narrative_x: An anonymous caller contacted  IAD and stated that Boston Police Officer Michael Geary posted questionable comments on Facebook. The caller E-mailed screenshots of the posts to IAD. The  screenshots display posts by a Michael Geary who, in commenting on a news article about Breonna Taylor posted; "Don't be a drug trafficker and you won't get shot by police. Believe it or not it really is that simple". Another post stated; She got exactly what she deserved. It's too bad her criminal boyfriend didn't catch a few rounds too...

The complainant who would like to stay private stated that on the FBI Facebook page, Officer Micheal Geary made the following comment: "rats get bats" in a way to entice violence to the post of the FBI seeking to identify individuals instigating violence in Washington, D.C.

Last night(Friday 7/22/22), I was followed and harassed by a Boston Police Officer multiple times in the South End. I do not feel comfortable giving my full information at this time, as the police officer tried to follow me home. I was told that all I needed to provide was a report and a contact. I did not get his badge number because the entire situation scared me and I was too shaken in the moment to gather this info. Nonetheless, I feel as though this incident needs to be noted as this was a clear misuse of power. Additionally, a description and license plate # is listed below. Interaction #1 ~7:00pm on Tremont St. & West Newton: I was walking down Tremont st, when said police officer approached me and asked me to stop walking. He was standing on the sidewalk near a construction zone. He first said "hi" as I was approaching him, to which I also said "hi" back, but kept walking. As I was passing him, the officer asked me to stop walking, to which I responded "why?". His response was "I'm just trying to say hi" & "I'm just trying to talk to you." in a very defensive manner, while throwing his hands up. I thought this was weird so said, "have a nice night" and continued on. He then got in his vehicle and started to drive down Tremont behind me. I noticed this and turned down a side st to get home. Interaction #2: ~7:20pm on Northampton st, near Mass Ave. I walked home, stopped at my apartment and am now walking my dog when I see a police SUV slowly pull down the same street, and then park across the way from me. He rolls down the window and immediately says "I'm a good guy". He then proceeds to step out of his vehicle and starts asking me a number of questions that become personal very quickly. I answered some, then stopped when they became inappropriate. Mind you, I was totally caught off guard by the fact this this police officer was now interacting with me 20min later in a completely different location and am shocked by the fact that he found me. He asked "Are you always in this much of a rush?" "What do you do for work?", "How old are you?", "Are you single?, "Are you dating someone?", "Do you ever have time to date?". I responded that I was not interested in dating and felt very uncomfortable having a uniformed police officer asking me these questions. He asked if we could grab "coffee" sometime and I said no. I then ask him why he was following me, if this was his territory and what his name was. He said that "it didn't matter". I told him that I needed to go and proceeded to walk away in the opposite direction, but it did not end there…I turn a corner and hide behind a parked car because I am worried he will see me again. I wait for a few min and I soon as I stand up, he's there... Interaction #3 ~7:25pm Camden St: This police officer pulls up to me AGAIN. He rolls down the window and sais "let me start over". At this point and my heart is racing. He gets out of his vehicle AGAIN and proceeds to say "So you're not interested in me?" & "You're not interested in dating me?", "You're not interested in any of this?" I say "NO, I am not interested in dating you or any of this" and then turn around run home. This police officer misused his power by following me down multiple streets to try and hit on me. Additionally, he chose to leave his post, drive around the neighborhood for ~20+min, until he found me. I DO NOT feel comfortable walking around my neighborhood now. I walk to work and am now fearful that this will happen again. If a uniformed officer feels this emboldened to follow a pedestrian and harass them multiple times, then this police officer must not fear any repercussions for his actions. That alone, makes me fearful to even report this event. This police officer willingly told me that he was 31yrs old. He is Black and ~6'3. He was driving a vehicle with the license plate #6556. I did not give this police officer my name. I would possibly, be willing to identify this police officer. Mr. Aime stated that he crashed Ms. Charles ' car in August 2025 and offered to pay for the damages, which Charles declined. Aime noted that Charles had gifted him a camera, but after they broke up, she wanted Aime to pay for the car damage or return the camera. Aime declined to do either. ¶ After declining, Charles; demand for the camera or money for the car, she and her cousin, Menrika Bertrand began sending him threatening messages, including, "let me catch you in person. Either give me the money or the camera, or I'm taking what I need. I'm going to have my coworkers escort me. ¶ On November 6, 2025, Charles and Bertrand came to his house. Charles told Aime’s mother that she wanted either the camera or the money for the vehicle. When Amie’s mother (what is the mother’s name?) asked them to leave her home, they complied but continued sending threatening messages. The pair stated that they would return to his house and attempt to break in to retrieve the camera. Aime told Charles she was no longer welcome on his property, to which Charles responded I don't care; I'm coming back ¶ The domestic investigation was assigned to Sergeant Detective Stephine Gaines of the Boston Police Domestic Violence Unit. She stated she interviewed Aime, and he stated that Charles made no specific criminal threats. Gaines will be closing out the domestic investigation involving Charles. ¶ Officer Charles' actions, however, violated Boston Police Rules and Regulations 102 Sec. 3 Conduct: Employees shall conduct themselves at all times, both on and off duty, in such a manner as to reflect most favorably on the Department. Officers briefly handcuffed and detained, Mr. Arnold Bernier of 603 Irving Road in Randolph, Mass. Officers frisked Mr. Bernier and his vehicle for a firearm with negative results. allegation_x: Body Worn Camera Deployment - Officer Responsibility
narrative_x: At approximately 7:30 PM, I received a distressing call from my 24-year-old son, informing me that my 15-year-old son had been struck by a police vehicle and had suffered a broken limb. To my shock and frustration, I was not contacted by law enforcement or medical personnel—despite the fact that my son is a minor with underlying health conditions due to being in remission. ¶ My son has no prior encounters with law enforcement, yet no one has provided a clear explanation for why such excessive force was used. He was simply on his way home with friends, adhering to his 8 PM curfew. While I am grateful that he is alive, this incident could have easily ended in tragedy, particularly given his medical history. ¶ I am outraged and deeply concerned about how the police are handling situations in our community. While I understand the importance of public safety, the reckless and aggressive actions taken in this case have left my child severely injured and traumatized. As a result, he now requires surgery, I must take multiple days off work to care for him, and I need to arrange counseling to help him process this traumatic event. Additionally, I must coordinate closely with his school to ensure he does not fall behind academically, as he is in his final year of middle school and already has frequent medical appointments due to his remission. ¶ The following is my son’s firsthand account of the incident: ¶ *“My friends and I pulled into Raymond Tire because we heard a noise coming from the scooter we were riding. The scooter was stalling, and we stopped to try to fix it. Suddenly, an unmarked black vehicle with no lights or sirens approached us, and undercover officers got out. As more officers arrived, I decided to walk away. I was on the sidewalk when a marked blue-and-white police cruiser hit me and ran over my foot. After that, I blacked out. The next thing I remember was being on the sidewalk in pain, yelling for an ambulance. I immediately called my brother so he could let my mom know what had happened. ¶ As I regained awareness, I overheard a white officer instructing someone to arrest me. However, the only Black officer on the scene refused, stating that I needed medical attention for my foot. I was left in pain for an extended period before finally being transported to the hospital.”* ¶ This incident is unacceptable. My child—an unarmed minor with a serious medical history—was struck by a police vehicle, left in distress, and nearly arrested instead of immediately receiving medical attention. The fact that law enforcement failed to notify me, his parent, only adds to the negligence and disregard for his well-being. ¶ I demand answers. I demand accountability. No parent should have to experience the fear, frustration, and anger that I feel right now. I will not rest until those responsible are held accountable for their actions and meaningful changes are made to prevent this from happening to another child. About 14:30 hrs., on 7/1/25, I received a report from Officer Dennis O'Rourke, who was working the front desk at D-14, for a complaint regarding an incident that occurred yesterday 6/30/25 at about 16:30 hrs.(#I252052884) where the complainant was listed as the suspect in a road rage incident.  Off-duty officer Hooker stated in the above incident report that the suspect was possibly armed with a gun and he overheard him say "bitch I'll shoot you" made references that "he kills cops". ¶ While taking the initial complaint Wardsworth became augmentative with officers at the front desk and threatened officers' Houtmeyers and O'Rourke saying "I'm going to get you and I'm going to get you to.  And I said calm down stop threatening my officers and I'll take the report. ¶ The complainant, Dominique Deville Wardsworth from 79 Walnut Park apt#1 Roxbury, MA 02119-1176, came into the lobby of D-14 to speak with a supervisor regarding an altercation he had with an off-duty officer he described as a light brown skinned male 5'8", slim build, braided hair, possibly Cape Verdean or Dominican.  He stated the incident first started when a car with tinted windows and a female driver was riding his bumper inches away while he was driving on Commonwealth Avenue near the Old Veterans Building now known as the Residences at Brighton Marine 1465 Commonwealth Ave.  He further stated that the female operator beeped her horn constantly at him until another car stopped directly in front of him. ¶ At this point, Mr. Wardsworth stated the off-duty officer who was in uniform pants, displayed a badge from around his neck, and pointed a black handgun at him.  He stated that he attempted to tell the officer what the female did wrong, and the officer said, " that's my girl, it doesn't matter that she's a female I'll shoot you, I'll kill you".  Mr. Wardsworth stated he responded saying "you isn't no cop you aren't acting like no cop". Wardsworth stated he began to argue with the officer yelling back and forth.  The officer said, "don't worry I'll see you, I'll see you" and then Wardsworth stated he said, "you're a coward you are acting like that with a gun I'll fight you right now".  Wardsworth stated the officer said, "we can fight" and put his gun away and got into a fighting stance, but when Wardsworth got out of the car to fight, the officer pulled out a handgun and put it in his face and said, "I'll blow your head off".  Wardsworth stated "if you're going to shoot me then shoot me" then the officer said, "get the fuck in your car, get the fuck in your car or I'll shoot you" and then slammed the door on his left hand as he got into the driver's seat.  According to the incident report, the suspect/complainant Wardsworth left the scene and was stopped by officers with body cameras on in Fidelis Way.  Boston Housing Authority located video footage of a female exiting the suspects' vehicle with a bag in her hand and enter into 31 Jette Court.  The suspect/complainant was reportedly combative with officers who were surrounded by a crowd during the verbal altercation.  Should be noted that Officers requested EMS to the scene to treat Wardsworth who initially became agitated and jumped out of the ambulance but was eventually transported later on according to the incident report. ¶ The area around 1465 Commonwealth Ave is known to have surveillance cameras and Boston housing Authority has video as well as officers with body worn cameras. Williams was arrested for resisting arrest, assault and battery with a dangerous weapon, and assault with a dangerous weapon. narrative_x: Officer Adilson Rosa submitted a Detail Authorization Record (“detail card”) that falsely indicated National Grid did not show up on August 24, 2020, at 653 Bennington St, East Boston.  National Grid provided documentation that shows they worked fixing a gas leak that day and could not verify that the customer signature on Rosa’s detail card was one of their employees.  Additionally, Officer Rosa did not submit his detail card within 96 hours.  His card wasn’t verified until 43 days later.  Officer Eliana Builes was also assigned to this detail. At approximately 9:30, I received a radio call from operations to meet a caller at Stuart St. and Tremont St., who wanted to make a complaint about an officer. I met complainant Jared Swett. Swett stated that he wanted to complain about an incident that had happened at the Customs House at 3 Mckinley Square that had happened about an hour previously.  Swett stated that he was sleeping in a window alcove of the Custom House and a police officer that he has had previous interactions with started yelling at him and then placed him under arrest. Swett complained that he had a prior injury to his shoulder, and as a result of the officer handcuffing him, he felt pain in his shoulder. H&H was called and arrived on scene.  When H&H arrived the EMT's advised Swett that they would take him to the hospital, but he wouldn't be able to bring his dog with him in the ambulance.  Swett stated he would seek treatment on his own. ¶ I, then went back to A-1 and looked up the incident that the complainant Swett was referring too and reviewed the Body worn camera footage.  The call was for a removal of person sleeping in window of the hotel. The body worn camera footage depicts Officer Calvin Ervin ID #76156 assigned to the A101A trying to wake up Swett several times.  Swett appears to be passively resisting Officer Ervin as he is giving him commands to stand up. Officer Ervin then tells Swett that he is going to place him under arrest and Swett still is passively resisting until Officer Ervin places him in handcuffs behind his back.   The suspect is then placed in the back of the BPD vehicle. The officers then request Animal Control for Swett's dog that is on scene. Complaint as received: ¶ On December 29, 2022, I, Sgt Mark Tobin, was performing my regularly scheduled first half shift. I am currently assigned to the Crime Scene Response Unit, Squad One First Half. ¶ At approximately 2130 hours I suspected and then discovered that Boston Police Officer Rory Coleman ID # 102172, was using his Boston Police Department issued cellular phone to unlawfully secretly record oral and video communications within the crime scene response unit. Officer Coleman was not present in the office at the time of this discovery. ¶ The cellular phone was left unattended on Officer Coleman’s workstation. I observed the phone actively recording and the current timestamp showed the device was recording in excess of one hour. ¶ I confiscated Officer Coleman's department issued work phone, which was ultimately turned off, placed inside a Faraday Bag and then secured inside gun lock box #4 in the Duty Supervisors Office. ¶ At approximately 2235 hours I advised Officer Rory Coleman in person (in the foyer outside the Crime Scene Response Unit) that I found his cell phone recording and confiscated it. I then relieved him of duty for the remainder of his shift and informed he would be notified with further instructions at a later time. Sgt Det Cazeau was also present at the time I relieved him of duty. Officer Coleman was not asked any questions during this interaction. Form 26 Completed. ¶ This complaint is being filed as a violation of the following Boston Police Rules and Regulations violation: ¶ Rule 102 Section 3: Conduct Unbecoming ¶ Rule 102 Section 35: Conformance to laws ¶ Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 272 Section 99 C Unlawful Secret Recording ¶ Complaint as received: ¶ On December 29, 2022, I, Sgt Mark Tobin, was performing my regularly scheduled first half shift. While attempting to make an arrest of an individual who was wanted on several warrants and was the subject of a recent Breaking and Entry that occurred on District 18, nights prior, Officer Nicholas Politss,opolou ID#157658, engaged in a brief foot pursuit of the suspect, Willis McGhee, DOB9/13/1970, who attempted to evade  arrest and in the process of scaling a chain link fence topped with barbed wire, in the rear of 1293 Hyde Park Av which is the rear of the Eversource Substation property. Officer Politsopolous provided verbal warnings to stop or he will be Sprayed with OC.  As the suspect scaled the fence, PO Politsopolous deployed a single burst of OC Spray toward the suspect prior to reaching the top of the fence.  He again deployed another burst of spray as the suspect was climbing over the barbed wire as he was about to climb back down.  The suspect was eventually placed under arrest and subsequently treated for his exposure by Boston EMS.  PO Politsopolous' decision to utilize his OC Spray, even though it could be warranted with the possibility of avoiding potential violence from a fleeing suspect while he was alone, the moment he deployed his OC Spray was unreasonable at the moment the suspect was climbing up and over the barbed wire fence.  The suspect could have sustained serious bodily injury as he could have snared himself on the barbed wire while he was incapacitated.  Rule 304, Section 5: paragraph 2: "Conversely, all officers should be aware of the potential, however limited, for serious injury arising from the use of an incapacitating agent."

allegation_x: Special Order 15-014 Timely Submission of Payroll Forms
narrative_x: As a result of a preliminary detail investigation that was conducted on Wednesday, January 5, 2022, into a questioned invoice by Accutemp Engineering with regard to Officer Eliana Builes, I performed another preliminary investigation with regard to an assigned detail for RJV Construction Corporation performed on August 23, 2021 at 4 Falcon Street on District A-7. ¶ A request for two officers was made by Mr. Victor Pacella, Project Manager, for RJV Construction.  The detail was assigned to Officers Eliana Builes and John Pels on the day of the detail, August 23, 2021.  The details were assigned at 08:25 hours and 09:45 hours respectively. ¶ Officer Builes submitted a detail card, tracking number 2441604, with a start time of 08:30 hours and an end time of 09:00 hours and marked the detail card “No Show” for a total of 30 minutes worked. ¶ Officer Pels submitted a detail card, tracking number 2441605, with a start time of 10:15 hours and an end time of 15:00 hours for a total of 4 hours and 45 minutes worked. ¶ Note: ¶ 1.	Officer Builes’ detail card was verified on October 6, 2021, 44 days after the detail was performed. ¶ 2.	Officer Pels’ detail card was verified on September 2, 2021, 10 days after the detail was performed. ¶ After reviewing the detail card submissions, I contacted Mr. Victor Pacella at RJV Construction about the assigned details.  Mr. Pacella stated that their records indicate that only one officer worked the assigned detail at 4 Falcon Street on August 23, 2021.  Mr. Pacella also stated the construction crew worked the entire day from 07:30 hours to 15:00 hours. ¶ Based on our conversation, I requested that Mr. Pacella document our conversation in writing on a department letter head, scan, and email to me.  Mr. Pacella was concerned about the response the RJV Construction would receive from police officers if he documented the reported issue.  I informed Mr. Pacella that the Boston Police Department would investigate any reported misconduct.  Mr. Pacella stated he would provide the requested letter with supporting documents. ¶ Officer Builes violated Section 23 of Rule 102 (Truthfulness). Officer Builes was Untruthful by submitting a detail card with the actual start time of 08:30 and an actual end time of 09:00 hours as true and accurate. Officer Builes was also untruthful by marking “No Show” on the detail card. ¶ •	Officer Builes’ detail card submission is in direct conflict to the hours worked by RJV Construction.  RJV started work at 07:30 hours and worked until 15:00 hours. Coupled with the fact ¶ that Officer John Pels did work the assigned detail. Officer Builes’ submission of a “No Show” detail card reflecting she performed the detail from 08:30-09:00 hours cannot be accurate ¶ giving RJV was on-site at 07:30 hours and Officer Pels arrived at 10:15 hours. ¶ Officer Builes violated Section 3 of Rule 102 (Conduct). Officer Builes’ Conduct was unbecoming as it did not reflect favorably on the Department. ¶ •	Officer Builes knowingly submitted the detail card with tracking number 2441604 with a start time of 08:30 hours and an end time of 09:00 hours. Mr. Pacella provided a letter stating ¶ their records only indicate that Officer Pels worked the assigned detail. Officer Builes’ conduct can be construed as acceptable behavior by contractor and the general public.  It gives the ¶ false appearance that a Boston Police Officer can submit a detail card and expect compensation for a detail that was not worked. ¶ Officer Builes violated Special Order 15-014 later re-issued under Special Order 18-031. ¶ •	Officer Builes did not submit the detail card for verification until 44 days after the scheduled detail date.  Officer Builes was required to submit her detail card within 96 hours (4 days). ¶ Officer Builes violated Section 7 of Rule 325 (Detail Cards). ¶ •	Officer Builes did not submit the detail card with tracking number 2467807 that accurately reflected the actual hours worked.  RJV does not have any record of Officer Builes working the ¶ assigned detail at 4 Falcon Street on August 23, 2021. ¶ Officer Builes violated Section 5 (Cannon 7 of Ethics) of Rule 113. ¶ •	Officer Builes submission of the detail card with tracking number 2467807 for indication that she had performed the detail, but not having performed the assigned detail at 88 Kingston ¶ Street on August 23, 2021 is a corrupt act. ¶ Officer Pels violated Special Order 15-014 later re-issued under Special Order 18-031. ¶ •	Officer Pels did not submit the detail card for verification until 10 days after the scheduled detail date.  Officer Pels was required to submit her detail card within 96 hours (4 days).

At about 17:11 hours on January 29, 2020 while assigned to the Bureau of Field Services, Night Command, I received a telephone call from Superintendent Marcus Eddings.  Superintendent Eddings informed me that a complaint had been received regarding a Detail Officer at Congress St/ Atlantic Ave. directing traffic while wearing white sneakers.  Superintendent Eddings further directed me to identify the officer, determine if the complaint was correct, and if so to initiate a BlueTeam Complaint against the officer. ¶ Using the BlueNote Detail system I identified the officer assigned to that location as PO Shayna Rivera, ID# 144503, assigned to District 1.  The Detail Vendor was Boston Properties, 280 Congress St.  I responded to that location and observed PO Rivera directing traffic in front of the garage exit.  PO Rivera was wearing a uniform knit cap, rain jacket yellow side out, uniform pants, and white sneakers.  I spoke to PO Rivera and inquired about the white sneakers.  She exclaimed “Oh My God, Captain, I am so sorry.  I was running late to the detail because of an arrest, I was in the K-Car, and when I got here, I forgot to put on my black shoes!  They are in my car right there, let me go put them on.”  PO Rivera then walked over to her personal vehicle which was parked at the curb, pulled black shoes out of the trunk and put them on. ¶ PO Rivera was in violation of Rule 306, Section 6, which specifies in relevant part: ¶ Shoes: ¶ ?	Low quarter, military style, black shoes of smooth leather or Corfam, with plain toes and ¶ laces; … ¶ Utilizing Rule 109, Section 5, I admonished PO Rivera to not forget in the future, and she assured me that the issue would not reoccur. ¶ Rule 109 Section 6 reads in relevant part:	Sec. 6 Oral Reprimands: Oral reprimands, given by supervisors for minor violations of the Rules and Procedures, such as improper uniform or reporting late for duty, are simply spoken censures or reproofs. While a notation that an oral reprimand was given is entered into the district permanent personnel record, no record of the reprimand goes into the permanent personnel file. The rule contemplates that such reprimands will be given on an informal basis without any form of prior notice. ¶ In conformance with my instructions from Superintendent Eddings, this Oral Reprimand is being entered in to the BlueTeam Systemin order to memorialize the infraction.

Mr. Hogan informed me that  a detective under my command had just conducted himself in an extremely unprofessional manner.  The detective was identified as Sexual Assault Unit Detective Jesse Goff.  Mr. Hogan relayed to me that Detective Goff had entered Boston Municipal Court seeking a phone search warrant. Two other clerks also attempted to assist and be helpful in rectifying the issues while attempting to gain clarity. I am submitting a formal complaint regarding the conduct of a Boston Police Officer identified as Officer Flores, Badge #4194. ¶ Date of Incident: November 20, 2025 at approximately 6:00 PM ¶ Location: Friend St., Boston, Massachusetts ¶ Context: Delivery access for Ascend (state-licensed cannabis dispensary) ¶ I work as a state-licensed cannabis courier delivering for Ascend through a third-party company. As you may know, Ascend has communicated repeatedly with the Boston Police Department regarding the ongoing utility work on Friend St. and the legal requirement for couriers to maintain vehicle access to the building. Under CCC regulations, transporting cannabis products through public streets on foot is both unsafe and non-compliant with state security policy. ¶ Despite this, tonight I witnessed Officer Flores speaking to my coworker in an unprofessional and concerning manner. Officer Flores stated that he “ran these streets” and that he could tow his vehicle or issue a ticket if he wanted to, implying selective enforcement of the law based on personal discretion rather than policy or public safety. ¶ This is especially troubling because: ¶ Multiple non-commercial vehicles were parked in the 30-minute loading zone and no-parking area, yet were allowed to remain there. ¶ I personally received a $90 ticket last week for parking in that same no-parking zone. ¶ Enforcement appears inconsistent and based on the officer’s preference rather than clear standards.

The TopMix bar and kitchen is a small establishment which is mainly known for their food, but they also have a bar inside the establishment. On the mentioned date, Zachary and myself took a table in the back portion of the location which is on the opposite side of the bar. We ordered appetizers and a meal and were watching the sports channel on the television. At some point during this, my brother Estevon Ribeiro arrived to TopMix and briefly conversed with us before he went to the bar with a friend of his from work. My brother had also asked if he can use my charger so that he can charge his phone. On Friday January 24, 2020, Captain Kenneth Fong, Commander of Area A, informed me of a complaint concerning Detective Steven McManus. Detective McManus was performing a paid detail for Chiofaro Management on Thursday January 23, 2020.  Detective McManus was photographed while directing traffic during the course of his duties. In the photograph, Detective McManus can be seen wearing pants that have a wide reflective stripe along the side as well as brown shoes with a white sole. This is in violation of Rule 306 Sections 6F (trousers) and 6I (shoes). Captain Fong instructed me to inform Detective McManus of this infraction, ascertain his explanation and to reprimand him verbally. On Monday, January 27, 2020, I spoke with Detective McManus, informed him of the complaint, showed him the picture and asked why he was not dressed in the proper attire as per the rule.  Detective McManus seemed embarrassed and contrite in his explanation. Detective McManus explained that he wore the reflective striped pants as an extra measure for visibility. Detective McManus explained that his function at this particular site is to halt traffic on Purchase Street and pull traffic from the parking garage as well as preventing back up and gridlock. Detective McManus further explained that when he left his house in the morning, he forgot his regulation black colored uniform shoes and only had the brown colored shoes he had worn earlier in the day. When I spoke with Detective McManus, I admonished him for being out of uniform and stressed the importance of being in the correct uniform of the day, not only for conformity, but for the importance of visibility and being easily identifiable to the members of the general public. About 10:45pm, on Wednesday 2/27/2020, Officers Lekaditis and DePina, in the CK01F, initiated a traffic stop of a stolen motor vehicle near the intersection of Morton St and Harvard St. ¶ Officers were on patrol of Blue Hill Ave (outbound) near the intersection of Deering Rd. when they observed a motor vehicle, a black Acura sedan bearing MA Reg: 3HTN31 (vehicle 1), double parked on Blue Hill Ave. As officers drove past the vehicle they observed that the vehicle was running and the vehicle was occupied with at least 2 passengers. A CJIS  query of the vehicle revealed a "Stolen Vehicle" status. The vehicle was reported stolen on 02/25/2020 out of 154 Standard St (see I202015273). Officers then observed the vehicle begin traveling inbound on Blue Hill Ave and make a left turn onto Morton St. ¶ Officers informed Boston Police Operations of the stolen vehicle and requested additional units to the area. Offices were able to catch up to the vehicle near the intersection of Morton St and Harvard St. ¶ At this time, the C431F (Boyle), got in front of the vehicle on Morton St. Officers then activated their emergency lights and initiated a stop of the vehicle. The vehicle attempted to flee at which point the vehicle drove into the rear of the C431F unit with force and fled down Morton St. Officers notified operations that the vehicle had struck a department cruiser and fled on Morton St. At this time officers did not know if Officer Boyle had sustained any injuries from the collision or the extent of the damage to the department cruiser (Vehicle #7533). ¶ Officers then continued after the vehicle, as it turned right onto Canterbury. The vehicle then drove through the red light at Canterbury St and American Legion Highway without stopping and turning left onto American Legion Highway (towards Blue Hill Ave). The vehicle then continued on American Legion Highway accelerating at a high rate of speed. ¶ The vehicle then made a left turn onto Blue Hill Ave (inbound), going through a red light without stopping,  and continued at a high rate of speed. As the vehicle drove through the area of Blue Hill Ave and Glenway St, officers observed the vehicle cross over into the outbound lane of Blue Hill Ave traveling the wrong way. The vehicle then continued to the intersection of Blue Hill Ave and Seaver St where the vehicle collided into a gray Honda sedan, bearing MA Reg: 1BAS58 (vehicle 2), which was traveling on Blue Hill Ave (outbound). Officers immediately notified operations of the accident. ¶ Officers were then able to remove the operator of the vehicle, later identified as Malik Martin (DOB 02/01/03), and the passenger, later identified as Deandre Dewhollis (DOB 9/24/00). Officers observed that both Martin and Dewhollis sustained injuries in the accident and were transported by Boston EMS (A2 & P2) to Boston Medical Center. A CJIS query of Martin later revealed that he did not possess an active driver's license. ¶ Officers also provided aid to the occupants of vehicle 2, later identified as Jonathan Lopez Gomez (DOB 2/14/96) and Rosangelis Ortiz (DOB 2/26/99). The vehicle was being towed to his mother's property because the registration was revoked for failing to pay the insurance. Mr. Taft stated that he was pulled over by Boston Police Officers in the area of Seaver Street and Walnut Ave in Roxbury. Mr. Taft stated that this occurred at approximately 10 pm. Mr. Taft stated that during this motor vehicle stop the officers advised him that the registration on the rental car he was driving had expired. Mr. Taft stated that while he did not initially believe the officers, they did show him proof of this. Mr. Taft stated that the officer then informed him that they would need to tow the vehicle. About 10:38pm on Wednesday 06/17/2020, Officer Beggan assigned to the F441F responded to a radio call for a Assault and Battery in Progress at the intersection of Hardy Street and East 8th Street, Boston. ¶ Assisting units on scene were the F411F (Brian Fitzgerald) and F431F(Arthur Fritch). ¶ Upon arrival, officers observed two males standing outside of 2 Hardy Street on the sidewalk. Officers also observed two females and a male on the sidewalk in front of 1 Hardy Street. ¶ Officers approached the two females and a male outside of 1 Hardy Street due to one of the females visibly upset sitting on the curb. Officer Beggan spoke with the reporting party, Mr. Brady DeAngelo, who stated he and his two friends arrived in the area of Hardy Street looking for a lost cell phone. Mr. DeAngelo stated they eventually were able to ping the location of the missing phone to the area of 2 Hardy Street. Mr. DeAngelo stated he and his two friends were continuously walking the premise around 2 Hardy Street then attempted to make contact with the residents. Mr. DeAngelo stated his two female friends began ringing the door bell and knocking on the front door. ¶ Officers then spoke to Ms. Alexis Aggouras, who was visibly upset while sitting on the sidewalk opposite 2 Hardy Street. When asked what had happened, Ms. Aggouras stated she lost her phone after spending the day at the beach and eventually pinged its location to the area of Hardy Street. Ms. Aggouras stated she and her two friends were looking under vehicles, in the street, and around the premise of 2 Hardy Street. Ms. Aggouras stated she believed her phone could possibly be inside the residence of 2 Hardy Street. Ms. Aggouras stated she repeatedly rang the doorbell and knocked several times on the front door in an attempt to make contact with the residents. After ringing and knocking on the door, an unknown male exited the front door of the residence and grabbed her and her friend in neck area. At this moment, the male began forcing Ms. Aggouras and her friend off of the stairs at 2 Hardy Street. Ms. Aggouras denied EMS on scene and stated she did not suffer any injuries.  While speaking with Ms. Aggouras, officers could smell a strong scent consistent with the smell of an alcohol beverage mixture emanating from her breathe. ¶ Officers spoke with Ms. Elise Rosen, who stated she was accompanying Ms. Aggouras at the front door of 2 Hardy Street. Ms. Rosen stated she and Ms. Aggouras attempted to locate Ms. Aggouras' phone by attempting to get in contact with the residents of 2 Hardy Street. Ms. Rosen stated she and Ms. Aggouras began ringing the door bell and knocking on the front door. Ms. Rosen stated after knocking on the door and ringing the bell, a male eventually exited 2 Hardy Street and physically grabbed her and Ms. Aggouras in the neck area. Ms. Rosen stated the male physically pushed her and Ms. Aggouras off of the front stairs, yelling in their faces. Ms. Rosen stated she, Ms. Aggouras, and Mr. DeAngelo separated from the unknown male and notified police. Ms. Rosen informed officers she and Ms. Aggouras spent a day at the beach and admitted to consuming alcohol throughout the day. ¶ Officers spoke to Mr. Daniel Fitzgerald, who stated he was suddenly woken up when he heard his doorbell being continually rung. Mr. Fitzgerald stated he then heard excessively loud banging, consistent with the noise of trying to gain access into a locked door. Mr. Fitzgerald stated he was unsure if someone was trying to break in. Mr. Fitzgerald stated he got dressed and quickly ran down to his front door to confront the excessive banging. Mr. Fitzgerald stated he opened his front door, in the darkness, and observed three unknown parties on the front porch of his property aggressively demanding for a cell phone.  The three parties began to yell, shout, and accuse him of stealing a phone while stepping closer towards the front door of Mr. Fitzgerald's residence. At this moment, Mr. Fitzgerald grabbed two parties, independently and attempted to escort them off of the property. Mr. Fitzgerald relayed that he verbally demanded the parties to get off his property as they continued to accuse him for stealing a cell phone. Mr. Fitzgerald stated he was able to escort the parties on to the public sidewalk outside of his residence. Mr. Fitzgerald stated the two females involved in the altercation were intoxicated and acting hysterically. Mr. Fitzgerald informed officers that the three parties stated they were calling police to which Mr. Fitzgerald responded "please do." Mr. Fitzgerald stated he was unaware of the situation regarding a lost phone and was concerned as to why three unknown parties were at his front door aggressively shouting and making false accusations. ¶ Officers spoke with Ms. Rosen a second time who stated a neighbor, who resides on the first floor apartment of 2 Hardy Street, stated he located a bag on his front steps. The neighbor, later identified as Mr. Lawrence Norton, stated to Ms. Rosen he located a cell phone in the bag but it was out of battery power. In order to attempt to locate the owner, Mr. Norton began charging the phone. While the phone was charging, Mr. Norton heard a loud commotion outside of his home and exited his residence. Mr. Norton eventually learned he was in possession of the lost phone, and was able to return it to Ms. Aggouras. Officers spoke with both Ms. Aggouras and Ms. Rosen who stated the phone was returned along with the bag it was left in. Both Ms. Aggouras and Ms. Rosen confirmed nothing from the bag was missing. Ms. Rosen also confirmed the phone was possibly dead or shut off due to not being able to ping the location of the phone right away. ¶ Speaking with Ms. Aggouras, Ms. Rosen, and Mr. DeAngelo officers offered to request Boston EMS on scene for a medical evaluation to which both Ms. Aggouras and Ms. Rosen denied repeatedly. Officers asked the parties where they would be staying for the night to which they replied Ms. Rosen's residence in Dorchester. Concerned with both Ms. Aggouras and Ms. Rosen being under the influence due to her own omission, officers offered to drive the parties home. Mr. DeAngelo informed officers he had his motor vehicle on scene. Mr. DeAngelo did not appear to be under the influence of alcohol and was in a safe condition to operate a motor vehicle. Prior to leaving the scene, Ms. Aggouras was visibly upset and stated "I'm sorry" several times to which officers informed her she had nothing to apologize for. Mr. DeAngelo and Ms. Rosen stated they were thankful for the officers on scene and proceeded to return back to Ms. Rosen's residence. ¶ It should be known there was an unidentified male on scene who did not wish to answer any questions. The unidentified male was a white male, about nineteen to twenty-two years of age, with curly dark hair, and a green shirt. ¶ I was notified of the incident after the officers had returned to the station. narrative_x: On October 10, 2020, ACD received an email alleging that there is often a marked Boston Police cruiser parked at 259 Bennington St. near the rear door of La Chiva Restaurant after closing time (3:00 am).  The complainant would usually see the unoccupied cruiser between 4:30 and 6:30 am.  La Chiva had recently hired C.I. Security for the late-night crowds.  C.I. Security was the subject of an unrelated ACD investigation. ¶ ACD initiated an investigation to determine the officer's whereabouts and if the officer had any involvement with C.I. Security.  ACD investigators conducted surveillance from October 13 until November 22, 2022, and received additional emails from the complainant on October 16 and November 14 with photos of a cruiser parked near La Chiva’s back door.  Investigators identified Officer Michael Forde, ID# 8847.  Forde is assigned to District A-1 and frequently works morning watch overtime in District A-7.  The investigation revealed that although Forde parked near La Chiva, he did not enter the restaurant.  However, investigators discovered that Forde was going into a residence located at 237 Bennington St., likely on the second floor, and taking his calls from there.  Sometimes, Forde would hold onto Code 19s in other locations while inside the dwelling.  The mailbox indicates the second-floor tenants are Karolina Posada and Brayan Ventura Posada. ¶ The investigation revealed no evidence of criminal activity on the part of Officer Forde.  However, it exposed the following potential administrative violations: ¶ On November 4, 2022, Officer Forde was assigned to the G416A on overtime.  Forde was inside 237 Bennington St. at 1:00 am on November 5 when he was dispatched to 53 Putnam St. for a fight (P220512063).  Investigators observed Forde walk to and enter his cruiser which was parked at 257 Bennington St. at the bus stop and drive toward Day Square.  At 3:10 am, Forde was dispatched to 336 Saratoga St. for a DVIP (P220512202).  A query of evidence.com revealed that Forde did not activate his body-worn camera at either call. ¶ On November 17, 2022, Officer Forde was assigned to the G201A on overtime with Officer Paula Pearson.  At 1:52 am on November 18, Forde and Pearson were dispatched to 142 Marginal St. for a BEIP.  During this call, neither Forde nor Pearson activated their body-worn cameras. ¶ On November 21, 2022, Officer Forde was assigned to the G425A on overtime.  At 12:43 am on November 22, Forde self-initiated a Code 19 over the air at Sumner St. and Liverpool St. (P220540855). At 01:21, investigators observed a marked cruiser pull up and park in front of 249 Bennington St.  Forde exited the cruiser wearing a black civilian jacket and black knit hat and walked toward 237 Bennington St.  Although he was inside this apartment, Forde held onto the Code 19 and was eventually cleared by the dispatcher at 3:06 am.  At 3:22 am, Forde was dispatched to 810 Border St. for a BEIP (P220540945).  At about 3:23 am, the interior lights turned on from the second floor of 237 Bennington St.  At 3:26 am, Forde exited the front door of 237, walked to his cruiser, and responded to the call with blue lights activated.  Forde did not activate his body-worn camera at this call. ¶ According to evidence.com, the last video Officer Forde recorded was on October 2, 2022. ¶ Based on the above information, I recommend that this case be referred to IAD for further investigation and potential administrative violations. ¶ On October 10, 2020, ACD received an email alleging that there is often a marked Boston Police cruiser parked at 259 Bennington St. near the rear door of La Chiva Restaurant after closing time (3:00 am). I came home around 3am on 3/19/22 to find a Ford Edge SUV, MA plate number 223 D70, parked in my driveway halfway on my lawn. I called two tow truck companies and was told they couldn't tow a trespass unless it was ok'd by BPD. I called the non emergency number and they told me they would send an officer out to my address. After waiting half an hour I called again. An officer showed up around 4:10. At that time I called the tow truck company, the officer made sure that I was willing to pay for the vehicle to be towed and I put the tow company on speaker so the officer could approve the tow. While we waited the officer ran the plates of the car and said they belonged to an older lady and I explained it was a young man who had walked out of the car when he parked on my property at 1:30pm. He then took his flashlight and looked inside of the vehicle and he noticed a police baton and other BPD gear in the back of the vehicle. When the tow truck finally showed up at 4:31am the off duty officer came down the stairs of 5 Crowell street which is across the street from my driveway. He greeted the officer that had responded to the call and when I asked why he was parked on my property his exact words were "calm down princess." At that point I became very upset because not only had the officer been trespassing on my property and parking his personal vehicle on my lawn, but he had the nerve to insult me when I asked why he was parked on my property. We exchanged some words and he got in the vehicle and took off. The officer that had responded to the call couldn't believe what had happened and basically told me to file a complaint as I had a picture of the license plate number. On Sunday, March 06, 2022, at approximately 1:40 am, Sgt. Det. Brian Leahy contacted Sgt. Det. Lucas Taxter and informed him that he had just observed Police Officer Matthew Morrissey in front of his home on Chickatawbut St. in Dorchester.  At the time, Officer Morrissey was under investigation by members of the Anti-Corruption Division (ACD), had been interviewed at ACD twice, and had just been placed on administrative leave hours earlier on the morning of March 5 by Sgt. Det. Leahy, Sgt. Det. Taxter, and Lt. Det. Sean Martin. ¶ Sgt. Det. Leahy stated that he observed blue lights coming through his windows approximately ten minutes earlier.  At approximately 1:34 am, Leahy looked out of his front door to see what had happened and observed a black pickup truck stopped in the middle of the street near the end of his driveway.  The vehicle then traveled backward toward Leahy’s front door, and Leahy immediately recognized the registration plate, Mass. Reg. 5BB135, and the vehicle to be the 2019 Chevy Silverado owned by Officer Morrissey.  From within the house, Leahy observed the operator roll down his window, and at that time, he could see that it was Morrissey behind the wheel.  Morrissey had parked the truck on the sidewalk directly in front of Leahy’s front door, facing on-coming traffic and in a no parking zone.  Morrissey’s vehicle was parked approximately ten feet from the front door of Leahy’s house, close enough to block the egress of anyone entering or exiting the home.  From this proximity, Morrissey remained and stared at Leahy, standing in his house behind a glass storm door for approximately one and one-half (1.5) minutes, and then drove away.  Morrissey did not say anything or exit his vehicle.  As Morrissey drove away, Leahy photographed the truck and registration plate with his cellphone.  Sgt. Det. Leahy did not confront Officer Morrissey during this incident. ¶ This was the third in a series of confrontations instigated by Officer Morrissey while he was being investigated for violating the City’s residency ordinance.  On October 26, 2021, Sgt. Det. Leahy was in his assigned department vehicle conducting surveillance of Morrissey from the nearly-empty parking lot of Venezia Restaurant at 20 Ericsson Street, Dorchester.  At approximately 9:05 am, Leahy observed Morrissey’s black Silverado drive toward him and stop about twenty feet away, facing him.  The Silverado then slowly drove past Leahy, turned, and parked perpendicular to him, where it remained for about two minutes.  Because of heavy rain and the Silverado’s tinted windows, Leahy could not see who was operating.  However, a subsequent investigation revealed that Morrissey queried Leahy’s registration plate at 9:08 am on CJIS using his cellphone.  It is believed that this was a counter-surveillance technique used by Morrissey to help determine the extent of the ACD investigation.  Investigators discovered that Morrissey inappropriately queried vehicles registered to him, his family members, and ACD approximately fifty-five times as a counter-surveillance technique. ¶ On November 5, 2021, Sgt. Det. Leahy was again conducting surveillance from 20 Ericsson Street.  As Leahy entered the parking lot at 7:13 pm, he observed Morrissey’s Silverado parked on Ericsson Street facing Walnut Street and the entrance of the lot.  Leahy parked his department vehicle in a parking spot and immediately watched the Silverado enter the parking lot and very slowly encircle his vehicle at least twice from the adjacent travel lanes.  The Silverado did not travel anywhere else in the lot and exited.  Again, due to the window tint, Morrissey wasn’t visible to Leahy.  However, this is the only vehicle ACD investigators have seen Morrissey operate. ¶ The incidents mentioned above have caused great concern for Sgt. Det. Leahy and his family.  While knowingly being investigated by superior officers assigned to the Anti-Corruption Division, Officer Matthew Morrissey deliberately attempted to harass, intimidate, and cause emotional injury to Sgt. Det. Brian Leahy, his family, and to some extent, other members of ACD.  Moreover, Officer Morrissey’s intentional actions on March 6, 2022, while in front of Sgt. Det. Leahy’s home was retaliatory and directly related to being placed on administrative leave approximately fifteen hours earlier. ¶ As a result, on Sunday, March 6, 2022, at about 8:00 pm, Sgt.  Dets. Taxter and Leahy met Milton police officers at 449 Pleasant St, Milton, and placed Morrissey under arrest.  Morrissey was transported to District C-11, booked, and charged with intimidation of a witness/police officer, c268 s13B. On July 10, 2021, Officer Randall Martin, ID# 131276, was assigned to the J201A in District E-13.  At approximately 4:30 a.m., he and other officers responded to a call for a person shot at 360-B Centre St, JP.  On arrival, Martin observed ballistic evidence and a blood trail leading from the front door of the building.  The shooting victim, Kevin Desruisseaux, was located by another officer a few blocks away. ¶ Martin knew this location housed an illegal after-hours nightclub owned and operated by his good friend and Academy classmate, Boston Police Officer McDermott, and Boston Public Health Commission (BPHC) Police Officer Luigi D’Addieco. ¶ While on the scene, Martin received text messages from McDermott, who was inside 360-B Centre St, refusing to open the door for the police. ¶ Martin also sent and received texts from D’Addieco, who was watching investigating officers from his vehicle parked across the street. ¶ Martin also knew Desruisseaux was a doorman at the club. ¶ Investigating officers heard voices coming from inside the building and needed to enter.  They did not know whether any suspects were inside.  They did not know whether any additional victims were inside.  The Patrol Supervisor requested SWAT. ¶ Approximately an hour after officers arrived, SWAT made a forced entry into the building and located dozens of party-goers holed up in the basement nightclub, including McDermott. ¶ Although Martin possessed vital knowledge regarding the shooting and the occupied after-hours nightclub, he did not share it with anyone at the scene.  Martin kept this information to himself while his E-13 colleagues, SWAT officers, and K-9 officers investigated, devised a plan, and forced entry into the nightclub. I, Sergeant Detective Cooks, was assigned a complaint by Superintendent Ciccolo concerning Officer Cox's inability to return to work. ¶ On November 25, 2024, Officer Cox was on MIS, extended sick leave, but working a secondary job delivering pizzas.  Documentation and video of Officer Cox delivering Pizza can be found in the Boston Police incident report 242100244. ¶ On March 4, 2025, Officer Cox was working a secondary job when he called for police assistance.  That incident is documented and video recorded in 252017241 ¶ On March 5, 2025, called for police regarding incident 252017241.  A supplementary report was made, and BWC recorded the response. ¶ On March 7, I observed Officer Cooks engaged in his secondary job. ¶ Note that in all the incidents that take place, Officer Cox is wearing the uniform for the restaurant he owns and works for. I pulled the cruiser to the left of this car and angled it infront of this car partially blocking its path. No sooner did I exit the cruiser to approach, the car sped off through the intersection. I demanded his license and registration. He yelled in response who are you? I replied, "the police" and again demanded his paperwork. What police? he argued. The Transit Police I replied. I asked a third time for his license and registration and informed him he would be subject to arrest if he did not comply. With this the operator put the car in drive and began to slowly pull away. It wasn't until I applied pressure on the wrist lock as a pain compliance technique did the subject put the car in park. I retrieved a Ma. license and Boston Police Id card from his right front pocket identifying him as Detective Robert Tully of Hanover, Ma. I inquired about weapons and he stated his department Glock was in the bag. After turning the ignition off and removing the keys, I checked the compartment area for weapons. I seated Mr. Tully in the passenger seat out of the elements. His department firearm was located in the trunk which I kept for safe keeping. I then removed the handcuffs and had Mr. Tully wait in his car. While conversing with Mr. Tully I now detected an aroma of alcohol on his breath. I notified duty supervisor, Sgt. Cantella of the situation and requested a supervisor from our agency as well as Boston Police to take charge of Mr. Tully, his department cruiser and firearm. Sgt. Roy responded to assist. Sgt Cantella informed me that Lt. Lanchester of C-11 was apprised of the situation. BPD. Officers Giannetti, Fogerty and Sgt. Brennan all from C-11 responded. During this time, Mr. Tully apparently could not wait had to take a bathroom break before this encounter was over. I issued Mr. Tully two citations #'s M1803359 & M1803360 for following too closely, passing on the right, reckless operation and refusal to submit, both criminal complaints issued in hand. On August 11th 2022, IAD was notified about an incident at Encore Everett involving Officer Rebecca Leo of BPD in which she is alleged to have committed a larceny from a found wallet on August 7 while at Encore Everett Casino.. ¶ A report was drafted memorializing the incident which reads as follows: ¶ 1. On Sunday, August 7, 2022 Sgt. Best entered an ACISS log note (22-13821) which indicated "EBH ¶ Investigations advises GEU of a cash theft that occurred at 0300 hours. Suspect picked up victim's ¶ wallet, removed $200 from it, then gave wallet to hotel registration and departed property. Investigations ¶ will attempt to contact suspect and contact GEU if additional assistance is needed." ¶ 2. On Monday, August 8, 2022, EBH Investigators contacted me after business hours regarding this ¶ same larceny. This larceny appeared to be handled in the normal course of manner by EBH ¶ Investigations with no GEU involvement besides GEU being notified. At this time, An EBH Investigator ¶ informed me that a member of the EBH Surveillance Team notified the Security Investigations Team ¶ that the larceny suspect was possibly a Boston Police Officer. This suspect had been previously ¶ identified by EBH Investigators as Rebecca Julia Leo 5/20/90. I advised the Investigator that I currently ¶ did not have access to review the video and I would review it on Tuesday, August 9 th . ¶ 3. The following day I located and viewed a video clip stored in the Surveillance Locker with a Clip ¶ Number of 34136 titled "Wallet Theft 31BZ07" and Incident ID of IN20220021105. The following is a ¶ summary of events I observed while watching video clips: ¶ · Camera 3198 @ 02:31:40 hrs. the victim's wallet falls from his left pocket. The victim is wearing a blue ¶ shirt and is wearing a baseball hat backwards. ¶ · Camera 3198 @ 02:46:48 hrs. Leo appears to see the wallet on the floor and picks it up. She then ¶ immediately opens the wallet and extracts a $100 Bill and has some interactions with the table dealer. ¶ · Camera 3198 @ 02:47:00 hrs. Leo leaves the table with the $100 Bill and Wallet in her left hand. ¶ · Camera 1 @ 22:47:19 hrs. shows Leo leaving the gaming floor and walking into the Main Lobby. ¶ 4. I then located and viewed a video clip stored in the Security Locker with a Clip Number of 34137 ¶ titled "Wallet Theft Suspect" with the same Incident ID as listed above. This showed multiple clips ¶ following LEO from the Main Lobby out to the Main Reception desk. The following is a summary of ¶ events I observed while watching video clips: ¶ · Camera 11553 @ 02:47:16 hrs. shows Leo manipulating the wallet with both hands and she then ¶ places her left hand into left pants pocket. She then appears to stuff her hand down into the pocket two ¶ times. ¶ · Camera 11379 @ 02:48:28 hrs. Leo approaches a Casino Bell Hop and retrieves what appears to be ¶ a single bill from her left pocket and hands it to the Casino Employee. Leo then hands the wallet to a ¶ female working in reception. ¶ · Camera 11380 @ 02:48:44 the Casino Bell Hop appears to make change for the bill in the amount ¶ of $95. He then secures Leo's checked bag and returns the $95 and bag to Leo. She then begins to ¶ leave the Main Lobby towards the South Elevators. ¶ 5. It is my understanding that the hotel employee who received the wallet reported that the wallet was ¶ empty and contained no cash when it was handed to her by Leo. The above is a summary of events ¶ and not all cameras and times are noted. ¶ 6. Silta was making the request, prior to providing the information, Sgt. allegation_x: Authorization & Use of Less-Lethal Weapons (2 counts)
narrative_x: On Wednesday, 12/11/24 Officers were called to 39 Warren Street, Roxbury for an EDP. Upon arrival Officers made their way to the 3rd floor to apartment 321 and announced their presence to the victim (Christopher Dooley). The victim instructed officers to enter his apartment and when officers opened the door they observed the victim to be sitting in an armchair with a kitchen knife to his chest. The victim had the tip on the knife pressed to his chest. The victim was slurring his speech and stated he had consumed alcohol today. The victim stated he was suffering from depression and that his family could not talk to him. Officers remained at the doorway and spoke with the victim in an attempt to de-escalate the situation. The B-2 Best team clinician responded and attempted to speak with the victim.  The victim was confrontational towards officers and the BEST team clinician. The victim stated that officers should not come into his apartment or it would not be pretty. The victim still had the knife pressed to his chest in an attempt to harm himself. Officers continued to talk to the victim to get him to put down the knife to offer mental health assistance. After exhausting all attempts to de-escalate the victim as well as offering mental health support officers requested a less lethal shotgun to the scene. Sgt. Det. Blando deployed the less lethal shotgun and fired 3 beanbag sock rounds. Officers observed the victim be struck twice with the beanbag less lethal rounds, one in the left arm and one in the stomach area. Officers immediately made entry into the apartment and seized the knife and placed the victim into handcuffs. ¶ The Firearm Discharge Investigation Team (FDIT) determined in their final report that Sergeant Detective Blando did not announce “Beanbag” before his discharge of the weapon, nor did he designate lethal coverage as required by Rule 303A.

narrative_x: I am submitting a formal complaint regarding the conduct of a Boston Police Department officer during an interaction on February 3, 2026, at approximately 10:00 PM, in front of 4 Ernest Ave, Hyde Park, MA (Hyde Park / East Dedham area). ¶ Due to winter conditions, snow removal was taking place, reducing a normally two-lane road to a single lane. I was behind multiple vehicles and could not see what was happening ahead. I waited for approximately 10 minutes without any movement or communication from the officer regarding traffic direction or the expected delay. ¶ At one point, the vehicle in front of me made a U-turn. The vehicle behind me then crossed into the opposite lane to continue and attempted to enter 4 Ernest St, which was not closed. I followed this vehicle cautiously to exit safely and avoid remaining stuck in traffic caused by snow removal. ¶ During this time, the officer stopped the vehicle in front of me and spoke with its driver longer than usual, then allowed all other vehicles in the normal traffic lane to proceed, leaving only myself and the driver in front held without explanation. Feeling stressed, frustrated, and wanting to go home, I briefly used my headlights to get the officer’s attention and calmly asked from my window, “How much longer are we going to wait?” The officer suddenly became angry and responded by yelling, “Whenever I want,” while allowing all other vehicles to pass. ¶ The officer then approached my vehicle with a hostile and accusatory attitude, demanding my driver’s license, while allowing the car in front of me—which initially drove in the opposite lane—to leave. I respectfully provided my license, which the officer took. He went to the other vehicle and took a long time before returning to me, continuing to allow other vehicles to pass while instructing me to stay parked in the opposite lane, not even allowing me to turn onto another street. ¶ After returning from checking my license, the officer also asked to verify my address and informed me that a citation would be sent to my home. When I asked for clarification, the officer stated, “You were driving the opposite way,” which is inaccurate, as I was only following the vehicle in front of me in a single-lane situation caused by snow removal. ¶ Throughout the interaction, I remained calm, respectful, and compliant. However, the officer’s behavior felt dismissive, unnecessarily authoritative, and intimidating. I felt singled out and unfairly treated without any legitimate reason. I also have a video recording and my vehicle’s license plate that verify my account. Additionally, I was not alone during this interaction. A female friend who witnessed the entire incident can corroborate my account of the events. ¶ My complaint is regarding the unprofessional, unfair, and intimidating conduct of the officer, not the potential citation itself. I respectfully request that this incident be reviewed and that measures be taken to ensure that community members are treated with professionalism and fairness.

Ms. Simone informed Officer Shoulla that a past known shoplifter, later identified as the suspect, Timothy Talbot, was currently in the dressing room with assorted merchandise.  Officer Shoulla immediately called for additional units to assist him. ¶ While waiting for backup, Officer Shoulla stood outside of the store at 149 Newbury Street to make sure he was able to observe the suspect in the store and be able to stop him if he attempted to exit.  Officer Shoulla observed suspect Talbot conceal an item on his person and exit the store.  As the suspect exited the store and prior to assistance arriving, Officer Shoulla stopped Talbot and advised him he was being stopped for shoplifting.  Officer Shoulla gave the suspect a verbal command to put his hands behind his back in order to be handcuffed.  Talbot actively resisted Officer Shoulla's attempt at gaining control and attempted to break away from his hold.  Officer Shoulla repeatedly informed Talbot that if he did not stop resisting, he would be sprayed with OC spray.  The suspect continued to actively resist which in Officer Shoulla deploying his department issued OC spray in the direction of the suspect to gain control.  After being sprayed in the eyes, Talbot was still able to break away from Officer Shoulla's hold and flee on foot without his jacket or shirt on.  Talbot was then located and arrested behind 28 Exeter Street after a foot chase.  Multiple other units, as well as walking beat supervisor, Lieutenant Pusey, responded to the scene.  Officer Shoulla informed Lieutenant Pusey that he failed to activate his body worn camera during rush to control and arrest the suspect. ¶ Officers requested EMS and Boston EMS (A93) arrived on scene to treat suspect Talbot for OC exposure before officers transported him to D-4 for booking. It was later revealed that the suspect had concealed on his person, 2 pairs of shorts and 5 pairs of pants from Alo, totaling $776.00 in value.

I respectfully report that Officer Bryan Augustine, I.D.# 148242, violated Boston Police Department Rules and Procedures, Rule 102, Section 10, Eight Counts. ¶ Officer Augustine called in sick on July 9, 15, and August 6, 2022.  He exhausted all of his sick time and vacation before July 9.  As a result, Officer Augustine was carried as AWOL for the above dates. ¶ On August 6, 2022, Officer Augustine called in sick at 11:37 PM, failing to provide sufficient time before the beginning of his shift. ¶ On August 14, 2022, Officer Augustine failed to report for duty on time and had to be woken up by a supervisor. ¶ On October 16, 2022, Officer Augustine failed to report on time for his regularly scheduled tour of duty and failed to notify a supervisor. ¶ On October 19, 2022, Officer Augustine called in sick after the start of his regularly scheduled tour of duty and was carried as AWOL. ¶ Counts 1, 2, and 3 - Officer Augustine violated Boston Police Rule 102, Section 10 - Unauthorized Absence from Duty, by calling in sick when he had exhausted his sick time and vacation time; attachment # 1 is (an email from John Brennan verifying the dates).  Officer Augustine had four personal days at the time of the absences but chose to call in sick. As a result, he carried AWOL for those dates.  He also violated Boston Police Department Rule 102, Section 10, Counts 4, 5, 6, and 7 by failing to report for duty on time. ¶ Count 4 - On August 6, 2022, Officer Augustine called in sick seven minutes prior to the beginning of his shift, not allowing reasonable and timely notice, attachment #2 (Sergeant DeFeo’s report). ¶ Count 5 - On August 14, 2022, Officer Augustine failed to report for duty at the start of his shift, 2345 hours, and had to be woken up by a supervisor, attachment #3 and #4 (Sergeant Swan and Sergeant Minichello reports). ¶ Count 6 - On October 16, 2022, Officer Augustine failed to report on time for duty again and did not notify a supervisor prior to being late, attachment #5 and #6 (Sergeant Swan and Officer Sosa’s reports). ¶ Officer Augustine filed a Form 26 concerning the August 14 and October 16 incidents.  He reported that he was late but did not provide a reasonable explanation as to why nor why he did not notify a supervisor, attachments #7 and #8 (Officer Augustine’s reports). ¶ Count 7 - On October 18, 2022, Officer Augustine failed to report on time for his scheduled tour of duty.  He called in sick at 2350 hours when his scheduled tour began at 23:45; attachments #9 and #10 (Audio recording and Sergeant Minichello’s report). ¶ Count 8 - Officer Augustine called in sick on October 18, 2022, without having any sick time available.  He was AWOL for the tour, attachment #11 (Absence Report) ¶ Officer Augustine received a notice of excessive sick time abuse by Captain John Greland while assigned to District 13 on February 27, 2020, warning him that continuation of sick time abuse may result in a suspension without pay, attachment #12 (Excessive Sick Leave Report). Officer Augustine has continually demonstrated a lack of attentiveness toward his time and attendance as a Boston Police Officer.  His current pattern is evidence of complete unawareness or total disregard for his actions, placing his fellow officers and the unit at risk. Therefore, in keeping with the concept of progressive discipline, I issued Officer Augustine a 1-day suspension. ¶ I presented Officer Augustine with the Notice of Suspension, BPD Form 0016-BFS-1005, on Thursday, October 20, 2022, in a meeting with Sergeant McGillicuddy and BPPA Union Representative Officer Conway.  He was also given a copy of M.G.L Chapter 31, Section 41, along with a copy of Boston Police Department Rule 102.  Officer Augustine waved his rights to request a hearing and signed the waiver.  His suspension will commence on October 22, 2022.
