On Wednesday, January 5, 2022, Denise Merlino assigned to the Paid Details Payment Unit informed me that an email was received from Timothy Halikias, Finance Coordinator, of Accutemp Engineering Inc stating the following: ¶ “Good Morning, ¶ I hope you are doing well. ¶ I am emailing you regarding invoice #BPD0098037. We originally requested two officers at 7am for this paid detail, but only one officer arrived at 9:30am and only one slip was signed according to the job foreman on site. We paid for the officer that arrived under invoice #BPD0097413, but now we are being billed for the 2nd officer that never arrived. ¶ Can you please help us with this?” ¶ I directed Ms. Merlino to forward the email to me, and I would contact Mr. Halikias to discuss his concern.  Prior to contacting Mr. Halikias, I found that the details in question were assigned tracking numbers 2467807 and 2467808.  The details were assigned to Officers Eliana Builes and Kato Francis respectively, and the scheduled start time for each was 08:00 hours, and the scheduled end time was 14:00 hours. The details were to be conducted at 88 Kingston Street on District A-1 on October 26, 2021. ¶ Both details were assigned the day of the detail. Officer Builes was assigned the detail at 08:47 hours and Officer Francis was assigned the detail at 09:19 hours. ¶ Upon review of the details, I found discrepancies with the submitted detail cards. ¶ 1.	The detail card submitted by Officer Builes has a start time of 09:00 hours, and an end time of 9:45 hours for a total of 45 minutes worked and the detail card is checked “No Show.” The ¶ detail card was signed with a signature of “Jenkins.” ¶ 2.	The detail card submitted by Officer Francis has a start time of 09:30 hours, and an end time of 14:00 hours for a total of 4 ½ hours worked. The detail card was signed with a signature of ¶ “Dante Defuria.” ¶ 3.	Officer Builes’ end time of 09:45 hours is after the start time indicated on Officer Francis’ detail card of 09:30 hours (15 minutes after). ¶ Note: ¶ 1.	Officer Builes’ detail card was verified on December 8, 2021, 43 days after the detail was performed. ¶ 2.	Officer Francis’ detail card was verified on October 28, 2021, 2 days after the detail was performed. ¶ After review of the detail cards, I contacted Mr. Halikias.  Per our conversation, he stated the Accutemp Engineering does not have an employee by the name of “Jenkins” and Accutemp Engineering only had one detail officer work on October 26, 2021. Mr. Halikias also stated that Officer Francis who performed the detail was released shortly after he arrived due to the crane work being completed and there was no longer a need for a detail, but Mr. Defuria, construction supervisor, signed Officer Francis out for the scheduled end time of 2:00 PM.  Mr. Halikias stated he would get the approximate time Officer Francis was released. ¶ I requested that Mr. Halikias document our conversation and submit it to me in an email. Mr. Halikias stated he would after he spoke with Mr. Defuria about Officer Francis’ end time and we concluded our conversation. ¶ On January 6, 2021, I received an email from Mr. Halikias that stated the following: ¶ “Good Morning Marcus, ¶ It was a pleasure speaking with you yesterday. ¶ I spoke with our Construction Supervisor, Dante Defuria Jr, who was on site on Oct 26 and signed the detail authorization record for Officer Francis. He provided me with the following information: ¶ •	We requested two police officers for the detail ¶ •	Officer Francis arrived at 9:30am and was on site for approx. 1.5-2 hours. He mentioned to Dante that he was late because he was out of district ¶ •	Officer Builes never arrived as far as we know and we do not have an employee with the first or last name Jenkins. We’re not sure why it was marked as a no show since we had workers ¶ on site starting at 6am until 2pm ¶ If you need any additional information, please don’t hesitate to contact me directly.” ¶ After reviewing the email, I again contacted Mr. Halikias with regard to Officer Francis being released early.  Mr. Halikias stated that he would address the end time specified on the detail card and the actual time Officer Francis was released.  I later received an email that stated the following: ¶ “Good Morning Marcus, ¶ It was a pleasure speaking with you yesterday. ¶ I spoke with our Construction Supervisor, Dante Defuria Jr, who was on site on Oct 26 and signed the detail authorization record for Officer Francis. He provided me with the following information: ¶ •	We requested two police officers for the detail ¶ •	Officer Francis arrived at 9:30am. He was on site until approx. 11-11:30am, but the detail authorization record shows an end time of 2pm. We were under the impression that we would be ¶ invoiced for 4 hours, but we were invoiced for 8 hours total ¶ •	Officer Builes never arrived as far as we know and we do not have an employee with the first or last name Jenkins. We’re not sure why it was marked as a no show since we had workers ¶ on site from 6am until 2pm” ¶ After reviewing the details in question and after corresponding with Mr. Halikias, Officer Eliana Builes knowingly submitted the detail card with tracking number 2467807 and checked “No Show” on the card and did not submit it to the appropriate detail clerk in a timely fashion (96 hours) as required under Special Order 15-014 and Special Order 18-031.  The detail card was received 43 days after the scheduled date of the detail for compensation. ¶ The vendor Accutemp Engineering has no record of Officer Builes performing the detail and the construction supervisor stated that he only signed the detail card for the officer that was present. If Officer Builes arrived at the assigned detail at 09:00 hours and signed out of the assigned detail at 09:45 hours, she would have been at the assigned location when Officer Francis arrived at 09:30 hours. ¶ Officer Builes violated Section 23 of Rule 102 (Truthfulness). Officer Builes was Untruthful by submitting a detail card with the actual start time of 09:00 and an actual end time of 09:45 hours as true and accurate.  Officer Builes was also Untruthful by marking the detail card that Accutemp Engineering was a "No Show." ¶ •	Officer Builes’ submitted detail card is in direct conflict with the detail card submitted by Officer Kato Francis and is supported by Mr. Timothy Halikias at Accutemp Engineering stating only ¶ one officer performed the detail at 88 Kingston Street on October 26, 2021. ¶ Officer Builes violated Section 3 of Rule 102 (Conduct). Officer Builes’ Conduct was unbecoming as it did not reflect favorably on the Department. ¶ •	Officer Builes knowingly submitted the detail card with tracking number 2467807 with a start time of 09:00 hours and an end time of 09:45 hours. Accutemp Engineering knowing only one ¶ officer performed the detail coupled with the fact the construction crew was on-site from 06:00 hours to 14:00 hours, caused Accutemp Engineering to question the invoice.  Officer Builes’ ¶ conduct can be construed as acceptable behavior by contractor and the general public.  It gives the false appearance that a Boston Police Officer can submit a detail card and expect ¶ compensation for a detail that was not worked. ¶ Officer Builes violated Special Order 15-014 later re-issued under Special Order 18-031. ¶ •	Officer Builes did not submit the detail card for verification until 43 days after the scheduled detail date.  Officer Builes was required to submit her detail card within 96 hours (4 days). ¶ Officer Builes violated Section 7 of Rule 325 (Detail Cards). ¶ •	Officer Builes did not submit the detail card with tracking number 2467807 that accurately reflected the actual hours worked.  Accutemp Engineering does not have any record of Officer ¶ Builes working the assigned detail at 88 Kingston Street on October 26, 2021. ¶ Officer Builes violated Section 5 (Cannon 7 of Ethics) of Rule 113. ¶ •	Officer Builes submission of the detail card with tracking number 2467807 for indication that she had performed the detail, but not having performed the assigned detail at 88 Kingston ¶ Street on October 26, 2021 is a corrupt act. ¶ As a result of reviewing the invoice in question with regard to Officer Builes’ detail card submission, it was discovered that Officer Kato Francis submitted a detail card that was not reflective of the hours worked. ¶ Officer Francis violated Section 23 of Rule 102 (Truthfulness). Officer Francis was Untruthful by submitting a detail card with the actual start time of 09:30 and an actual end time of 14:00 hours as true and accurate. ¶ •	Officer Francis’ submitted detail card is in direct conflict with the statement by Mr. Timothy Halikias at Accutemp Engineering stating that Officer Francis was released between 11:00-11:30 hours. ¶ Officer Francis violated Section 7 of Rule 325 (Detail Cards) ¶ •	Officer Francis knowingly submitted the detail card with tracking number 2467808 with an ending time that was not reflective of the actual time he was released and submitted a detail card ¶ with an 09:30 hours start and an 14:00 hours finish time. Mr. Halikias stated that Officer Francis was released at approximately 11:00-11:30 hours. ¶ •	Officer Francis’ detail card should have reflected working a maximum of 2 hours worked for a minimum of 4 hours paid.  By allowing his card to reflect 4 ½ hours worked, he was paid for 8 ¶ hours worked. ¶ Officer Francis violated Section 5 (Cannon 7 of Ethics) of Rule 113. ¶ •	Officer Francis’ submission of the detail card with tracking number 2467808 for indication that he had performed the detail until 14:00 hours, but having been released between 11:00-11:30 ¶ hours at 88 Kingston Street on October 26, 2021 is a corrupt act. ¶ Officer Francis violated Section 7 of Rule 325 (Detail Cards). ¶ •	Officer Francis did not submit the detail card with tracking number 2467808 that accurately reflected the actual hours worked.  Mr. Halikias at Accutemp Engineering stated Officer Francis ¶ was released prior to 14:00 hours. ¶ Officer Francis violated Section 3 of Rule 102 (Conduct). Officer Francis’ Conduct was unbecoming as it did not reflect favorably on the Department. ¶ •	Officer Francis knowingly submitted the detail card with tracking number 2467808 with a start time of 09:30 hours and an end time of 14:00 hours. Dante Defuria, construction supervisor, ¶ released Officer Francis between 11:00-11:30 hours but signed Officer Francis’ detail card for a 14:00 hour end time.  Officer Francis’ conduct can be construed as acceptable behavior by ¶ contractor and the general public.  It gives the false appearance that a Boston Police Officer can submit a detail card and expect compensation for hours not actual hours worked.

On July 20, 2022, the Boston Police Anti-Corruption Division received a complaint regarding a Phoenix Communications paid detail at the intersection of Cambridge and Bowdoin Street on Area A-1. The detail was scheduled from May 16, 2022 2000 hours until 0400 on May 17, 2022. The assigned officers were Sergeant Detective Carl Blando, Office of Homeland Security and Sergeant Detective Daniel Pusey of the Audit and Review Division . Blando was assigned the Phoenix Communications detail (Tracking #2547918) by the Paid Detail Assignment office at 1517 hours on May 16, 2022. ¶ Investigation: ¶ The investigation included a review of the submitted complaint - a seven-page BPD Form 26 from BPD Superintendent Marcus Eddings and a flash drive containing BTD camera footage. This was followed by an ACD interview of Sgt. Det. Carl Blando. The flash drive included footage from several different cameras in the City of Boston's traffic monitoring system. ¶ The camera located at Cambridge and Bowdoin Street revealed that Sgt. Det. Carl Blando arrived to the detail at 19:55.  Sgt. Det. Daniel Pusey arrived at the detail location at 20:03:43.  Sgt. Det. Pusey remains on-scene for a few minutes and then joins a different Phoenix Communications crew at another location which is working in concert with the Cambridge and Bowdoin site. Blando remains at Cambridge and Bowdoin for the entirety of the detail. ¶ Video showed Sgt. Det. Blando remain at the intersection of Cambridge and Bowdoin Street until his detail card is signed by Phoenix Communications supervisor, Michael Jenson. Blando drives away from the site at 00:01:01. The traffic cameras reveal that Blando performed the Phoenix Communications detail for a total of 4:06. Sgt. Det. Daniel Blando submitted and received payment for a detail card for 5 "actual hours worked." The submitted hours worked were from 2000 on May 16, 2022 to 0100 on May 17, 2022. ¶ Interview: ¶ Sgt. Det. Blando was asked if he could specifically recall a Phoenix Communications detail he performed on May 16, 2022 at Cambridge and Bowdoin Street. He stated he could not, Blando quickly added that he completes an average of five to six details per week. When informed that he worked the detail with Sgt. Det. Daniel Pusey he stated that it sounded a little familiar but that he had performed "six to eight" details with Pusey over the past year. He then pointed out that this detail was about nine months ago and it was difficult for him to remember specific facts.  He then added that he works the day shift and when he has a detail that starts at seven or eight in the evening he usually arrives early. He explained that he lives far from the City of Boston so he usually waits at work and then arrives early to his detail assignment. This is evidenced on the BTD traffic camera covering Bowdoin and Cambridge Street. I informed Blando that video showed him arrive to the detail on May 16, 2022 at 7:55 p.m. and depart at 12:01 a.m. on May 17, 2022. Blando and his attorney (Dunlap) reviewed screenshots taken from the traffic video of his arrival and departure. ¶ Sgt. Det. Blando reviewed the copy of his detail card for the job in question and answered that all of the writing appeared to be his. He stated that when a detail ends early he usually rounds the end time off "in fifteen-minute increments." He explained that he could not recall if the Phoenix Communications supervisor directed him to write in the 1:00 a.m. end time. However, he added that he knew that he had worked in excess of four hours "so he didn't see it as a difficulty because you're getting paid for eight hours regardless." ¶ Sgt. Det Blando stated that after his last detail related interview with ACD on June 30, 2022 he began keeping notes on the back of the pink copy of his detail card. The detail card, officially known as the Detail Authorization Record, comes in triplicate. The top yellow copy goes to the Paid Details Payment Unit, the middle pink copy is the officer's copy, and the bottom white copy is the customer copy. Blando described his personal note-taking process. He stated that he keeps notes on when he leaves the jobsite to use get dinner or if the crew changes their location. The Phoenix Communication crew did not leave the Cambridge and Bowdoin Street location to perform any work. They briefly relocated to A and Iron Street, South Boston (as shown by BTD video) but the crew does not set up or work. The Phoenix Communications workers merely pull to the side of the road and park for approximately a half hour while a different crew finished their work for the night. ¶ Sgt. Det. Blando stated that since performing this detail he became aware of a memorandum or email put out by Superintendent Marcus Eddings authorizing minute for minute pay on paid details. According to Blando he now puts minute by minute times on his detail cards. ¶ ACD 1 ¶ Superintendent Marcus Eddings conducted an audit on a paid detail performed on 1/21/21, by Sgt. Det. Carl Blando. Superintendent Eddings states that Phoenix Communication worked from 19:07 hrs. to 21:10, for a total of 2 hours and 3 minutes. Superintendent Eddings said that Sgt. Det. Blando submitted a detail card 19:00 to 23:15. Indicating he worked 4hrs and 15 minutes. ¶ ACD 2 ¶ Superintendent Marcus Eddings audited a detail performed by Sgt. Det. Carl Blando and Det. Nina Jefferson, on April 13,2022, at the intersection of Arch Street and Milk Street. Superintendent Eddings alleges that Sgt. Det. Blando submitted a detail card with a start time before his arrival. and an end time later than his departure. ¶ ACD 3 ¶ Superintendent Marcus Eddings audited a PV Barone paid detail performed by Sgt. Det. Carl Blando, and Officer Nicholas Beliveau on May 5, 2022.  Superintendent Eddings alleges that Sgt. Det. Blando submitted a detail card with inaccurate start and end times. ¶ ACD 4 ¶ Superintendent Marcus Eddings audited a Feeney Brothers detail performed by Sgt. Det. Carl Blando on May 10, 2022. Superintendent Eddings alleges that Sgt. Det. Blando submitted a detail card with an inaccurate start and end time. ¶ ACD 5 ¶ Superintendent Marcus Eddings audited l Feeney Brothers detail performed at 1200 Tremont Street by Sgt. det. Carl Blando. Superintendent Eddings alleges that Sgt. Det. After Mr. Ng completed his appointment, he left the building, but later return to get his passport ID.  Officers had switch positions at this point.  Mr. Ng explained to me that a white officer told him that badge cost $35 dollars and would be responsible for the lost.  Mr. Ng stated that for 25 minutes he emptied out his pockets, and empty out his backpack.  At one point nonwhite officer referred to him as "slow, and not all in the head", which sparked Mr. Ng to file a report considering he has dealt with depression and mental health struggles in the past. According to Mr. Ng the officer did not provide it because the officer told him that he (Mr. Ng) was in the wrong.  Mr. Ng stated he asked for the badge and number at around 2:12 pm - 2:15 pm.  Mr. Ng describe one officer a white male, 30-40 years old, glasses, bald, no facial hair.  The second officer was non-white, maybe Hispanic, light skin, braids, mustache, glasses.  Mr. Ng also emailed April Davies (Director of HR).  Below is the email that was sent. ¶ Dear April, ¶ Today at 11:20 am, I entered the police department to check-in for my physical. I successfully complied and passed through security check. I walked to the front desk, completed the sign-in form, showed him my passport ID to ask for access to the medical department. The officer, who assisted me, had glasses, a mustache, and braids. He simply directed me to the license desk to get a photocopy of my ID. ¶ After I received my photocopy of my passport ID, I showed it to the officer and he just gave me back the paper back without a badge. He directed me to the third floor and go all the way to the right. I asked for a repeat of instructions because it was hard to hear through the glass and the mask. I went through but the alarm rang. It was probably because I never received a badge so I tried to ask for it and the officer just told me to go through to the elevator. The white officer at the front desk told me that I cannot get my ID unless I have the badge to the medical department. However I was never given a badge. I did not even know what color the badge looked like because I was never given one. The officer then stated that I was lying and accused me of going to the second floor by accident. I never did that. ¶ The officer, with braids and glasses, told his fellow officer that I did receive a badge and that I was not all there in the head. That offended me greatly because I struggled with mental health problems in the past and I felt like he was belittling me as someone who had a mental deficit. The officer then walked away. ¶ It was now 2:05 pm and the officers refused to give me my ID. The white officer stated that the badge costs $35 and I could be responsible for this charge. The white officer then told me to take everything out of my bag, my jacket, jean, and shirt pockets. I did so because they were the police. I had no other choice. After 2:20 pm, the white officer told me that I could leave. I wanted to get their names and badge ID but they did not show these items to me. ¶ I finally left the department and I was crying on my way home because of what had happened. I would like to know where I could file this report because this was just not okay. ¶ I apologize for the inconvenience and thank you for taking the time to read this email. ¶ Sincerely, ¶ Wesley Ng

Mr Donovan was operating MA reg/458KF8 a silver Acura 32TL which was also described in the BRIC bulletin. ¶ Sergeant Kintigos advised the officers that he was behind that vehicle at the intersection of Old Colony and Dorchester St and the the suspect was aware of his presence.  Mr Donovan began speeding down Old Colony Ave heading inbound while going through every red light he approached.  Sergeant Hynes and Sergeant Connolly joined in on the pursuit with lights and sirens activated and observed the suspect drive over the sidewalk at D St and Old Colony Ave to avoid being stopped by the police.  The suspect took a right hand turn onto W Seventh St continuing to drive through red lights and stop signs until the officers were advised to discontinue pursuit by Sergeant Hynes for public safety concerns.  During this pursuit the officers observed a dog was in the backseat flailing around the vehicle because of the operators reckless driving. ¶ Minutes later Lieutenant Perkins received a phone call into the base that John Donovan came into Michael Flaherty's election office located on East Broadway threatening his entire staff.  The suspect left the building and headed toward the Stop and Shop parking lot.  Sergeant Hynes observed the suspect walking toward the parking lot and advised the officers nearby to block the suspect in so he could not drive off.  Officers Steele and Goggin in the F602D/F603D units and Officers Hill/Cox in the FG01D unit both parked their department vehicles behind the suspects vehicle so he could not back out.  The suspect put his vehicle in reverse and rammed into the officer's cruisers multiple times.  The officers approached the suspect's vehicle and broke the window in an attempt to stop the operator. Almost immediately, the officer pulled out a ticket pad. I opened the passenger door and offered to move the car. He refused and said he was writing down the license plate. He is within his rights to write a ticket. However, someone had been parked in the exact spot we pulled into and was out of the car. This man appeared to be friendly with this officer and did not receive a ticket for parking in the same spot. The officer appeared to be showing off for the mall security staff. They were laughing and joking. He wrote the ticket, which is his right to do, but felt rather arbitrary. Without my permission or consent, he opened the closed door to my car. I was assigned as the Duty Supervisor (LA04 Lt Brendan Walsh) for the First Half Shift at E-18. Lt. Edward McCarthy of Boston EMS/Health and Hospitals (785 Albany Street tel 617-343-1144) came to E-18 at about 1830 hours to file a complaint against Officer Dwayne Jackson (ID #011526). Lt McCarthy reported two of the EMT's he supervises, Robert Donovan and Casey Knowles stated to him Officer Jackson refused to ride in the back of the ambulance during transport of a female EDP who was under the influence of crack cocaine. The EMT's both told Lt McCarthy the female EDP (Ms. Kenyatta Starkes DOB 2-14-1984) was acting in a hostile/combative manner at the scene of the sick assist call at 50 Roanoke Road in Hyde Park. They stated they were both concerned for their safety and asked Officer Jackson to ride in back. They stated Officer Jackson refused to do so and said he would follow behind and assist them if needed. Lt. McCarthy stated they then attempted to transport the female to The Faulkner Hospital. They reported at some point during the transport the female became assaultive and struck EMT Robert Donovan in the forehead with a backhand strike. The strike caused a small cut/laceration to the middle of Mr. Donovan's forehead. EMTs reported they pulled the ambulance over and with the assistance of Officer Jackson they were able to get the female under control. They reported they again asked Officer Jackson to ride in the back of the ambulance for safety reasons. They stated he refused saying ' we are nearly there'. ¶ Lt McCarthy reports both EMTs said shortly before they were pulling into the wagon bay the female bit EMT Robert Donovan on his forearm. Lt McCarthy showed Lt Walsh photos he had taken of both the injuries to Mr. Donovan with his department phone. I advised him to save the photos. The injuries were clearly visible in the photos and the forearm injury was consistent with a human bite with teeth marks clearly visible. Lt McCarthy informed Lt Walsh he would be completing an injured on duty report for EMT Robert Donovan. The EMTs said when they prepared to transport the female form the ambulance into the emergency room they requested Officer Jackson handcuff her. Lt McCarthy states he told them he would seek flexy cuffs from Faulkner Hospital Security Officer. They reported the security guard (David Westin tel 617-983-7677) did not have any flexy cuffs. Lt McCarthy reports the EMTS with assistance from EMTS Kevin Pywell and John Markoast were able to secure the female into a room in the emergency area. Lt McCarthy stated EMT Donovan request Officer Jackson include the injuries in his report. He states Officer Jackson replied saying 'It will be in the report'. Lt McCarthy state he and the EMT's thought it was unreasonable for Officer Jackson to not assist them by riding in the rear of the ambulance. The original incident report was written by Officer Linda Mendez who was assigned o the call with Officer Jackson. I had approved the report at about 1730 hours. The report did not contain EMTs injuries. It was unclear if Officer Jackson had spoken with Officer Mendez about the two assaults by the female. The officers had worked a day shift and had gone home for the day. I directed Officer Drew Pokrant who was working a first half shift to write a supplemental to document the assaults on EMT Donovan. ¶ I was assigned as the Duty Supervisor (LA04 Lt Brendan Walsh) for the First Half Shift at E-18. On Sunday, December 11, 2022, there was an incident involving Sergeant DeFeo, I.D. # 11598, and Officer Augustine.  Officer Augustine was scheduled to work his regular Day Tour on December 11, 2022.  At 7:45 AM, Sergeant DeFeo called the Front Desk and spoke to Officer Murphy, I.D. # 131263, and inquired if Officer Augustine had arrived to work.  Officer Augustine had not.  He arrived around 8:20 AM, according to Sergeant DeFeo’s report. ¶ Sergeant DeFeo proceeded to the Front Desk to challenge Officer Augustine and have him file a report concerning his tardiness when he noticed Officer Augustine's motor vehicle.  Sergeant DeFeo stated in his report that he had addressed Officer Augustine about the tint on the front windshield two previous times, and Officer Augustine failed to correct the issue.  Sergeant DeFeo proceeded to issue Officer Augustine a motor vehicle citation.  During that exchange, Sergeant DeFeo requested a B-2 officer to report to headquarters in order to assist with recording Officer Augustine’s motor vehicle with a Body Worn Camera.  Officer Kerrigan, I.D # 148281, responded.  Sergeant DeFeo issued a motor vehicle violation to Officer Augustine and filed a report concerning the incident. ¶ Officer Augustine met with Lieutenant DiGirolamo and Sergeant McGillicuddy on Monday, December 12, 2022.  According to Lieutenant DiGirolamo and Sergeant McGilliuddy's reports, Officer Augustine expressed concerns over being targeted by Sergeant DeFeo.  He argued that other police officers are late for work and have tinted windows on their personal vehicles, yet they are not addressed by Sergeant DeFeo.  Officer Augustine had photographs to prove his point.  Officer Augustine also alleged that Sergeant DeFeo used profanity while addressing him, and the situation made him feel uncomfortable coming to work.  Lieutenant DiGirolamo did provide Officer Augustine with a copy of Rule 114 and explained the complaint process.  Officer Augustine deferred until a later date. ¶ I recommend IAD investigate this incident due to the allegations by both parties.  Officer Augustine has chronically failed to report to duty on time and received a 1 day-suspension from me on October 19, 2022.  His lack of attentiveness toward the essential requirement of arriving to work on time shortly after receiving a suspension is alarming and demonstrates that he did not learn from the discipline he received.  Additionally, I have received reports from Officer Augustine's immediate supervisor, Sergeant Swan, I.D. # 80402, expressing his concern with Officer Augustine's decision-making. ¶ The accusation made by Officer Augustine against Sergeant DeFeo must be addressed. (see I#222079943). ¶ The caller/ victim, Jaquelyn Giblin, informed the 911 call taker that her husband Gerard Giblin was being aggressive and was throwing items in the house. She also advised the call taker he had left home. ¶ On arrival, Mrs. Giblin was outside the residence and met the Officers in the driveway as Officers attempted to ascertain information about what had occurred. Mrs. Giblin immediately requested that she not be recorded (referencing the Officer's Body Worn Cameras). Mrs. Giblin stated, "I want to cancel any audio or video recording, please." At this point, the Officer informed BPD Operations that they would be Code 29. Mrs. Giblin reported to the Officers that her husband had left in his truck, but she wasn't sure of the registration plate information. The Officers obtained the registration information from a registry check through CJIS via the MDT in the cruiser. ¶ Mrs. Gibllin stated that he started throwing things about the house, broke a door, punched a picture causing the glass to break, and knocked over a heater on the back deck. Upon entering the residence, the Officers observed that the house was in complete disarray. The Officers observed clothes, food items, broken glass, knocked-over furniture, and a towel with what appeared to be blood in the kitchen, living room, and hallway areas. Mrs. Giblin informed the Officers that her husband had injured his hand during his outburst. Mrs. Giblin informed the Officers that their children, a six-year-old son, a three-year-old daughter, and an eight-month daughter, were present when he had his outburst, but she was not sure exactly where they were or what they saw during the incident. Mrs. Gibllin stated that at no time did her husband put his hands on her or the children. Boston EMS was requested for a well-being check of the children. Boston EMS 3A18 (Mellace/Decarlo) responded. ¶ The Officers Broadcast the motor vehicle's description as a black 2015 GMC pickup truck bearing MA Reg#VB6486 for officers in the area, advising that he was injured and may need an evaluation. The following units responded: Captain K. McCormick (YB03), Sergeant Detective Turner (V967), Sergeant Detective Gallarelli (V957); Sergeant Detective Joseph (X918), Detective Carrio (E810), and Detective McIntyre  (E811). Mrs. Giblin was informed of her 209A Rights. The Department of Children and Families was notified of the incident, and a 51A was filed. ¶ . On January 5, 2023, Probationary Police Officer Randy Do, ID# 112230, accepted detail tracking #2648556 for Daniel Cavalier LLC, at 232 Clarendon St.  The detail was scheduled for January 7, 2023, from 10:00 - 14:00.  At approximately 09:16 on January 7, Officer Brian Lydon (D-4 Detail Clerk) modified the time to 11:00 - 15:00 at the request of the vendor and notified Officer Do. (See notes in Blue Team) ¶ At about 11:15 am on January 7, Daniel Cavalier received a call from Officer Do, who informed him that he was his detail officer for 232 Clarendon St.  Cavalier was around the corner at 129 Newbury St at another job site and told Do he would be there when he was finished.  At about 11:45 am, Do approached Cavalier at 129 Newbury St.  Cavalier offered to sign Do’s detail card.  Immediately after signing it, Do said, “I gotta go.”  Cavalier said, “What?  I thought you were going to do my [other] detail.”  Despite accepting the 11:00 - 15:00 detail, Do replied, “I got things I gotta do,” and walked away.  Officer Ismael Almeida, who was the 129 Newbury St detail, asked Cavalier why he signed Do's card, and he replied, “I didn’t think he was going to do that.  I was just getting the formality out of the way.”  Cavalier subsequently worked at 232 Clarendon St without a detail officer. ¶ ACD investigators interviewed Cavalier. On June 1, 2023, I spoke with Colleen Alvarez who is an investigator from the Medical Examiner's Office.  She stated the ME's Office tried for several months to have Detective Sean Deery reply to them regarding an unclaimed person from a sudden death.  On May 31, 2023, an email was sent to District 1 detective supervisors and Detective Deery sent an email that she found disrespectful and unnecessary.  She stated this has been on-going issue with Detective Deery for 2 months with the ME's Office attempting to reach Detective Derry in order to be able to bury the unclaimed person from the sudden death.  Sergeant Detective Cellucci spoke with Colleen Alvarez, and she forwarded a copy of emails, an exhaustion letter and the emails sent to Detective Derry, as well as she has documentation of phone calls made to him that were not answered.  She stated she felt his response was an attack on the ME's Office, unprofessional, disrespectful and are now included in work product related to the unclaimed person.

On Saturday Feb. 25, 2023 CPT McCormick responded to a motor vehicle accident involving an off-duty Boston Police Officer, Stephen O'Connell (ID# 102668.) The accident was on Massachusetts State Police jurisdiction. They were/are the primary investigating department. PO O'Connell was transported from the scene to BMC for a serious head injury. CPT McCormick did notify IAD through Operations. He stated that he did observe a "white claw" can in the crashed motor vehicle. Sgt. Det. Moore (IAD) did respond and coordinate with MSP. He later obtained to MSP reports about the crash. PO O'Connell was determined to be in violation of MGL C89 S4A (Marked Lanes Violation) and MGL C90-9B (Unregistered Motor Vehicle). Reports uploaded. CPT McCormick also submitted a Form 26 about the incident. This is uploaded as well.

allegation_x: Pursuit Driving - Updates to Operations Division
narrative_x: On Sunday October 3, 2021 at about 0823 hrs Officers Ralph Blain (I.D. 153156), Raymond Soto (I.D. 148244)and Jasmany Beato (ID 1482244) engaged in a motor vehicle pursuit in which two people were injured as the result of a car crash. Officer Blain observed individuals he believed of unlawful design and the vehicle had no license plate affixed per state law (VAL). Officer Blain called officer Soto and asked for assistance. Officer Soto and Beato arrived to assist and effect a traffic stop for the VALS. The vehicle fled the area. Officers Beato and Soto followed this vehicle down Magnolia St. to Quincy St. At the intersection the suspect vehicle crashed into a third party vehicle. The operator of this vehicle (veh #3) was injured. Officer apprehended and arrested for failure to stop for police officer on scene. The operator was also found to have several warrants. The operator was also inured. Both injured parties were transported for medical care. 212071349 ¶ On Sunday October 3, 2021 at about 0823 hrs Officers Ralph Blain (I.D. 153156), Raymond Soto (I.D. 148244)and Jasmany Beato (ID 1482244) engaged in a motor vehicle pursuit in which two people were injured as the result of a car crash. He asked if he could take the car.  The officers asked if he had a license and he stated that he only had a permit; however, he was with a fried who had an active license.  That friend (Dellon Giles 6/22/2006) was queried, and it was confirmed that he had an active license.  They were then given the keys to the car. ¶ Back at the booking area, the officers advised Rodrigues that they had spared him the tow and given the car keys to his brother. The officers were unclear if he was being dishonest, messing with them, or telling the truth.  Nonetheless, they sought out to look for the vehicle.  Another unit located the car about 2 blocks away from Giles' home address (near Ripley and Vassar).  There was apparent damage to the vehicle. allegation_x: Courts - Failure to appear when summonsed.
narrative_x: On this day, I was assigned as the Y906 Supervisor of Cases in Roxbury Court.  ADA Mauve Healey came to my office to inquire whether Officer Jairo Polanco (C-11) signed into court.  She was expecting him to appear and testify (summons attached).  I told her that I would try to contact him and get back to her.  After confirming that the summons was emailed to Officer Polanco, I contacted the district where he works (C-11). ¶ I called District C-11 x4330, identified myself and asked the male who picked up the phone if he could get me a phone number to reach Officer Polanco because he was needed for court.  He told me that he would call Officer Polanco and tell him to call me at x4378.  I don’t know who picked up the phone, but it should be on a recorded phone line.  After some time, ADA Healey returned to my office and I realized that I had not yet heard back from Officer Polanco.  This time, I called the Duty Supervisor’s line at C-11 and asked for Officer Polanco’s phone number.  When I got the phone number, I called Officer Polanco and left a voicemail telling him to call me back ASAP, that he was summoned to court.  A male called on my phone line, that appeared to be the same number I contacted.  But, when I picked up and asked if he was Officer Polanco, he said, “No, I don’t know what you’re talking about.”  I asked him if he’s saying I dialed the wrong phone number, and he said “yes.”  We hung up the phone. ¶ I called District C-11 again and spoke with Officer Jade Cheek, who confirmed the phone number for Officer Polanco that I called earlier, as initially provided by the supervisor.  She stated that they had to call Officer Polanco four times, and they finally just spoke to him. The supervisor shall request that Operations make all appropriate notifications including the Firearm Discharge Investigation Team. ¶ An off-duty officer discharging a firearm in the City of Boston shall immediately notify an Operations Division Supervisor. On Sunday, March 7, 2021 at approximately 2120 hours, Mr. Strecker was dispatched by Security Control Center (SCC)to the On-Deck Burger Bar for a report of 4 Patrons who were verbally abusive and argumentative towards EBH staff. ¶ On Deck Burger Bar Manager Michael Misilo (#107975) called SCC for Security to respond to the Burger Bar for 4 patrons who were swearing at him because he was attempting to explain the Safety Policy for Covid-19 and advised them that they were not allowed to enter the Burger Bar with a drink from the casino floor. Burger Bar Manager Misilo advised me that the four patrons were walking around the bar drinking with no masks on and not obliging to the 6-foot distance between patrons' per safety policy. Security Manager Church and Security Supervisor Santos approached Kearney, Maimone, A. McDonagh, and B. McDonagh. Kearney immediately started swearing at Supervisor Santos on arrival. Supervisor Santos engaged in a conversation with the patrons (See attached statement). Manager Church engaged in conversation with Burger Bar Manager Misilo and then engaged in conversation with the patrons (See attached statements). The four individuals appeared to be highly intoxicated and refused to show any ID. As Kearney was talking, because his mask was down, I could smell the alcohol on his breath. I also observed that B. McDonagh was leaning on the Bar for support to stand as Security Management was conversing with the ¶ patrons. As Supervisor Santos was talking to Kearney, Maimone entered the conversation stating, "You guy's can bring all the suits you want up here, hell bring the cops too." Kearney stated, "Yeah, bring more Suits up and the cops too, I don't give a sh*t." ¶ Security Manager Church called SCC to dispatch the Gaming Enforcement Unit ¶ (GEU) at approximately 2127 hours. ¶ Supervisor Santos advised Kearney that he was causing a disturbance and asked if he could depart property for the evening. Kearney replied, "F*ck you guys, call whoever you want, call the troopers too." Supervisor Santos ¶ began moving the chairs as he was talking to Kearney to create the proper distance for safety policy regarding Covid-19. Kearney refused multiple times to depart property and explained that we had no grounds to tell him ¶ to leave and stated "you can't make me do sh*t, you can't do sh*t." Supervisor Santos then told Kearney to stand up and exit the restaurant again. Kearney continued to refuse. ¶ At approximately 2128 hours, Supervisor Santos advised Kearney of the Encore Boston Harbor Trespass Warning. Kearney stated, "Under what grounds, you can't f*cking trespass me, you have no authority to trespass me." ¶ Supervisor Santos then asked the other three patrons, Maimone, A. McDonagh, B. McDonagh to also depart the restaurant. All three patrons refused and B. McDonagh stated, "We are staying with him." Supervisor Santos told them ¶ they would all be trespassed if they did not exit property, to which A. McDonagh replied, "We already said, we leave when he leaves." ¶ At approximately 2131 hours, Supervisor Santos then advised Maimone, B. McDonagh and A. McDonagh of the Encore Boston Harbor Trespass Warning. A. McDonagh turned to Kearney and stated, "You good now?" Kearney replied ¶ with, "Yeah, f*ck these guys, let's go." As we exited the On Deck Burger Bar, Kearney turned to Manager Church and Supervisor Santos and stated "F*ck you two little d*ck b*tches." ¶ At approximately 2133 hours, GEU Sgt. Conant, Tpr. Caranfa, Tpr. Stowe and Tpr. Fogarty arrived on scene at the bottom of the escalator next to The On Deck Burger Bar. GEU was able to retrieve the ID's of the four patrons, ¶ which is when Kearney advised us that he was a Sgt. in the Boston Police Department and that the other three patrons were police as well. Kearney, Maimone, A. McDonagh and B. Mr Sohnis reports that Officer Williams told his daughter that she could pick up the report at Area D4, Boston Police Headquarters, or at Officer Williams' home. At some point that afternoon (between 3&4) Ms Nuriya Sohnis called Officer Williams and met him at his home. I went over to help Christina with RSW out of Gate 21 along side Fawad and Aody. Fawad, Christina and Aody were dealing with seating issues, I was handing out PPE (personal protection packs) to each customer as they boarded. ¶ Towards the end of boarding, jetbridge became backed up. Couple stood beside me. I asked the gentleman, who I now know as Mr. Morris, to kindly pull up his mask as it was by his mouth. For a moment I thought he didn’t hear me because Fawad was complimenting his wife’s shoes. I asked him again as boarding resumed, and Mr. Morris stated “I will pull up my mask, when you loose weight.” Stunned, I asked what? He said you heard me, “ I will pull up my mask, when you loose weight.” ¶ Fawad at that time heard Mr. Morris say this and asked him to step aside. This is when Mr. Morris proceeded to curse and created an scene in front of other customers. To the point where customers were cautious to board. When Mr. Morris learned that he would not be flying today, he shoved/ pushed me and Christina of the way and made his way on jetbridge. We blocked him from entering the plane. There were even customers on the jetbridge who wanted to make sure I was safe from him. We needed to close the boarding door to ensure that he would not make his way onto the jetbridge once more. ¶ Apparently, he was upset over a seat issue that I had nothing to do with/ knew nothing about as I was only there to hand out PPE. His behavior was uncalled for and for him to act this way over a seat issue is rude/ assaultive and  frightening. ¶ Sent from Sarah Zani on 10/27/2020 @ 4:pm via her cell phone to Lt. Det. I, Lt Gary J Ryan submit the following report. ¶ On November 13th, 2021, Officer Sequan Sparks-Clancy worked a day tour at Area D4. He was assigned as the DD96D (front desk). At approximately 8 am, Officer Sparks-Clancy informed the Duty Supervisor (Sergeant Hogardt) that a woman had come into the station wishing to speak to the supervisor. allegation_x: Body Worn Camera Deployment - Officer Responsibility
narrative_x: On Monday, February 23, 2026, Officer Freeman, operator, and Officer Lopez, observer, assigned to the J201D unit, received a radio call regarding a domestic violence incident at 2 Brewer Street, Incident #262015582. Officers left the district’s parking lot and proceeded down Green Street toward Amory Street with the wagon’s emergency lights activated. The officers had the green light and entered the intersection of Amory and Green Street when their vehicle was struck by a white Freightliner SD, Mass Reg MB961, City of Boston plow truck, traveling outbound on Amory Street. The head of the plow struck the front end of the department wagon. Neither officer’s BWC recorded the accident. Their BWCs were only activated after the accident. ¶ Officer Freeman stated in his report that his BWC was in the process of turning on, which he cited as the reason it did not record the incident. Officer Lopez did not provide any explanation in his report. Boston Police Department Rule 405, Sec. 3.1 requires officers to turn on their BWC immediately following Roll Call and for it to remain on for the duration of their shift. The officers received the 911 call around 11:20 AM, midway through their shift. Both Officers should have had their BWCs turned on and ready for recording before receiving the call for service. About 1:50 pm on 4/26/24, Officers from C-11 responded to a 911 call for a disturbance involving an off-duty Boston Police Officer at 2 Neponset Ave in Dorchester.  C-11 officers spoke with off-duty Officer Roland Robinson who stated that he had an argument with his stepson and brandished his firearm during the incident.  Robinson's stepson, Tyler Powell left the scene and went to his father's house and reported that Robinson pointed a firearm at him and pushed him.  Powell was uncooperative with the officers but advised them of cameras in the building.  Investigators from the Domestic Violence Unit were able to view the video surveillance from the hallway of 2 Neponset Ave and observed Roland Robinson draw his firearm and push Tyler Powell into the stairwell area.  Robinson was placed under arrest at the scene and charged with Assault by means of a Dangerous Weapon to wit: Firearm and Assault and Battery. ¶ About 1:50 pm on 4/26/24, Officers from C-11 responded to a 911 call for a disturbance involving an off-duty Boston Police Officer at 2 Neponset Ave in Dorchester. At about 1:06 pm on Friday, January 20, 2023, Officers Manning & Gentile, assigned to the C202D, received a radio call for a report of a person with a gun at 492 Harvard Street, Apt. 1, Dorchester. ¶ Upon arrival, officers spoke with the victim, Angela Horton, who stated that her sister’s boyfriend, Dion Webb (D.O.B.: 07/22/1974), came into her bedroom and pointed a long revolver-type firearm at her. Horton stated that Webb was still inside the front bedroom of the apartment and that he was alone in the bedroom. Officers secured the interior and exterior perimeter of the apartment and requested the Boston Police District B-3 Patrol Supervisor, Sergeant Rooney (C902), and the Boston Police S.W.A.T. gun car to respond. ¶ Sergeant Rooney declared a Code 99, and the Boston Police S.W.A.T. team arrived on the scene shortly after that. The Boston Police S.W.A.T. team breached the bedroom door of the apartment and placed the suspect, Dion Webb, under arrest. On Wednesday, 04/05/2023, The HK01F (Officer Ty Clark ID #162323 & Officer Thomas Garvey ID#162948) was involved in a department motor vehicle accident at the intersection of Park Street and Dorchester Ave., Dorchester (#232026400). The HK01F was responding to a priority-one radio call (P#230163350/I#232026401) when they entered the intersection and struck MA REG #3NEA65, which then slid into MA REG #2GMC67.  Both officers and three individuals from the other vehicles were transported to various hospitals.  All three vehicles sustained damage and were towed from the scene.  Preliminary reports indicate that HK01F may be responsible for the accident, which resulted in multiple injuries and damage to vehicles.  Awaiting on the Department motor vehicle and injured officer reports from the responding patrol supervisor to make final determination. Based on a tip, ACD investigators conducted surveillance of Officer Shawn Marando from February 10 to February 24, 2024.  Marando partnered with Recruit Officer Feliz Penalo in the G101A each night.  Investigators observed the officers to be very proactive.  They regularly conducted traffic stops, enforced parking ordinances, and volunteered to take pending calls.  They regularly took Code 19s near the bars at closing time and conversed with citizens, merchants, and security personnel from the various licensed premises.  Investigators found no evidence to support the allegations in the tip. ¶ However, analyzing the G101A’s activity revealed several problematic matters.  This is especially true when RO Feliz Penalo’s probationary status is considered. ¶ There were several incidents where the officers did not properly document their interactions with motorists and other citizens, did not notify citizens they were being recorded, and did not dock their body cameras in a timely manner. I respectfully report that on  03/14/2022 , at approximately 7:15 AM, I responded to 17 Augustus Av, relative to an active protest taking place in front of the Mayor's residence.  I requested Area EDT's from E-5, E18 and E13 to assist at 17 Augustus Av  Upon arrival I observed approximately six protesters with signs standing at the intersection of Crandall Street at Augustus Av.  These individuals were, also, yelling their grievences towards the Mayor's residence.  I further observed one (1) female banging a on container.  I approached this female and advised her not to bang on the "drum".  I then began to advise the protesters that they can hold signs and yell but they can no longer use amplification devices and Bull Horns, bells and whistles.  I further stated that if they continued using these items that there is possibilty of a criminal complaint application being sought for disturbing the peace.  I further advised the protesters that no one would be arrested and no devices would be seized. Several times during my statement, Sgt. Shana Cottone interupted me and stated her displeasure with what I stated previously about amplification devices and other noise devivces.  Shana Cottone then advised me and both officers and protesters on scene that my statement was unlawful and violates free speech.  As time passed, several more protesters arrived on scene till there were now approximately 16.  It should be noted that with the arrival of more protesters , the use of Bull Horns and whistles took place.  I observed several protesters including Sgt Cottone using the "Bull Horn' when directing their grievences at the Mayor's residence. Finally, The Mayor and her husband along with their two young children exited their residence and proceeded to walk down Augustus Av onto Poplar Street towards Roslindale Sq   Some of the protesters began to follow the Mayor and her family down the street. At this point, I directed several officers to walk with the Mayor and her family.  A short way down Poplar Street, the protesters stopped following the Mayor and returned to 17 Augustus Av.  At no point was there any physical contact between the Mayor , her family and the protesters.  The entire incident was captured by the BWC of the Police with J201 & J416A )  A incident report was written by P.O. The following narrative was taken from Boston Police Report I# 222003233: ¶ At about 3:20 PM on Saturday 01/15/2022 Officers Aragones and Dowling in the D201D responded to a radio call for a protest at 1330 Boylston Street (Regina Pizzeria) Boston, Ma. ¶ The following is summary of the events that took place not a word for word account: ¶ Upon arrival officers met with the store manager (Kenneth Johnson) who stated that a group of females came into the store and sat down and wanted to order food. Mr. Johnson stated he then called the police to remove the group due to them not following the new mandate. ¶ Officers then spoke to the group that consisted of Ms. Shana Cottone and 5 unknown females who refused to identify themselves. The group stated that they were not going to show proof of vaccination and that they bought one bottle of water. Officers spoke to Mr. Johnson again who stated that one of the workers handed Ms. Cottone a bottle of water assuming she would go pay for it at the register. He stated that she did not pay for the water at the register and there is no record of her purchase of the water. Officers attempted to obtain video surveillance to which Mr. Johnson stated the cameras were not working. Ms. Cottone stated that she put $2 in the tip jar for the bottled water. Officers asked the group to leave the restaurant several times and refused. Officers then requested a patrol supervisor to the scene. D909 (Wright) arrived on scene and spoke with the group. The group again refused to leave and officers stated that they were remaining on scene until the group left the premises. An unknown male then dropped two pizzas off to the group at their table and then left the restaurant. Officers Aragones and Dowling were then relieved at the scene at about 4:10PM by the DT55F (Keaton) and the D499F (Antonino) still accompanied by the D909. I respectfully report to you, an interaction that occurred on October 26th, 2023 with Officer Erik Shears, where his demeanor was unprofessional, disrespectful, and insubordinate. At approximately 8:00 PM I called Officer Shears to order him for a 4PM shift. I informed Officer Shears that I would have to order him for a shift tomorrow to which he replied, “back to back?” I said “yes sir, unfortunately we have to do that”. Officer Shears went on to question how he could be ordered as the detail room said he was “all set”. I informed Officer Shears  that overtime trumps details and that he would need to kick in his detail. Officer Shears replied that he had something to do with his daughter and that he was told he was all set. I once again informed Officer Shears that he was ordered and that overtime takes precedence over details. Officer Shears again questioned me saying “yeah, not back to back, you can’t do that?” At this point with four others to be ordered, I told Officer Shears that if he needed explanation on how the to-be-ordered list works, he could come to the DS office and I would explain it to him. Officer Shears quickly said he would be in and I asked how long he would be, Officer Shears replied, “five minutes”. ¶ I felt that Officer Sears was confrontational on the telephone so in anticipation he might continue on this path, I proactively contacted Officer Canto, the on duty BPPA union rep, and informed him that Officer Shears had an issue with being ordered and requested Officer Canto to assist and witness this effort. ¶ Approximately 15 minutes later Officer Shears arrived at the A-1 DS office. Officer Shears entered the office and asked what was going on. I rolled my chair over the desk closest to the office door and remained seated, and placed the to be ordered list on the desk. I began by saying the list is done by hours and his name was next. Shears questioned why there were so many people in the office for this. I replied that Officer Canto was a union rep and that it was his job to explain the list if needed, and also that Sergeant Detective Cellucci and Sergeant Plunket, who were previously in the DS office, could witness the conversation, if needed. Shears took an aggressive stance and stated in a confrontational tone, “you’ve had a problem with me since before you had stripes from that thing out there” (see summary of incident below). I replied that I had no issue and that ordering was done from a to-be-ordered list and once again tried to explain the list to him. Shears raised his voice and said, “no, you've held a grudge against me since then”. I disagreed and stated I held no grudge and asked if he could cite one example of a situation to verify that accusation. Shears quickly changed the subject and said, “I was told I was all set, I have the messages”. I replied, once again, details have nothing to do with getting ordered, there is a list. Shears interrupted me, once again raising his voice, stating that “he had texts from the detail room” and reached for his telephone. I informed him that a police officer may have told him that he was all set, but I was a Sergeant and I was informing him that he was next on the list and was ordered. Shears continued that he has no issues with anyone and that I was holding a grudge. At this time Sergeant Detective Cellucci stated to Shears “You’re aware he’s a Sergeant”?, Shears answered, Yes. “You understand you’re ordered”?, Shears answered, Yes. Sergeant Detective Cellucci then told Shears to leave the Office. ¶ During this conversation, Officer Canto attempted to slow Shears’ responses seemingly so that he would respect the rank and understand the message I was attempting to relay. Shears seemed “locked on to” me and persistent to continue with his insubordinate attitude. I remained seated and calm during the entire conversation, however Shears continued with his confrontational stance, questioning and accusing me of holding a grudge the entire time. ¶ – ¶ Below please see summary of previous incident mentioned in paragraph 3. ¶ I respectfully report that on June 19th 2023 while assigned as a patrolman in area A-1, I had an encounter with Officer Erik Shears that unbeknownst to me would turn out to be a confrontation. While in the report writing room I suggested that Officer Shears, whom I referred to as “new guy”, give a new cruiser to Officer Mundo as it was his birthday. At that point I had been assigned to A-1 for approximately 21 months and had never seen Officer Shears, thus jokingly referring to him as “new guy”. Officer Shears immediately squared his body to me and in a confrontational tone, asked who I thought I was talking to, to which I stated I was talking to him. He stated something to the effect that he was not new and questioned why I thought I could “disrespect him”. I immediately replied that I meant no disrespect and held out my hand to shake his and introduced myself as Josh. Officer Shears replied “Shears” and grabbed my hand squeezing it extremely tight to the point where I pulled away and said “wow, that's quite the handshake pal, you don't have to squeeze my hand like that”. He replied “that's my handshake”. I continued that it was a bit over the top and that he was overreacting to something that was not meant to offend him. Shears continued with his confrontational stance and tone to the point where Officer T. Ostholthoff spoke up from his computer station something to the effect of, Hey man, (Shears) I don’t know your name but I’ve worked with you a few times and you’re messing with the nicest guy at A-1, he meant no disrespect and you should stop. Shears continued that I should not have called him “new guy” and disrespected him in front of people. Otsholthoff informed Shears that from his point of view I meant no disrespect and that he should stand down. Shears continued to argue, to the point that Officer Erb asked him to leave the report room and guided him to the exit door. ¶ As a result of Officer Shears’ unprofessional behavior, disrespect, and insubordination, I find Officer Shears to have violated Boston Police Rule 102 Section 9.

At Approx. 02:30 AM on July 14th 2024, Sgt. MacDonald along with myself (Sgt. Gomes) were requested to speak with two parties in the District B-3 lobby, located at 1165 Blue Hill Ave. ¶ Mr. Juan Ayala-Powell (DOB: 07/13/1989) along with Ms. Leyla Pizarro (DOB: 12/25/1991) had arrived at District B-3 to speak with Supervisors in regard to a recent interaction with Boston Police Officers on a Traffic Stop in the area of 200 Harvard St., Boston MA. Mr. Ayala Powell stated to Sgt. MacDonald that they were pulled over by Boston Police Officers for no reason, pulled out of their vehicle, and assaulted. Mr. Ayala-Powell stated that he wanted the names of the Boston Police Officers involved in the incident, as well as their badge numbers. Ms. Pizarro then requested to be evaluated by EMS. Boston EMS was then requested to respond to District B-3. Ms. Pizarro was transported to the Carney Hospital for the abrasions to her knees. ¶ While Sgt. MacDonald was reviewing Body Worn Camera footage of the incident. I (Sgt. Gomes) had gone to speak with Mr. Ayala-Powell in regards to the incident. Sgt. MacDonald returned a short time later, also to again speak with Mr. Ayala-Powell. During this time of Mr. Ayala-Powell giving his narrative, Sgt. MacDonald informed him of several discrepancies regarding his accounts from the incident compared to Body Worn Camera footage. Sgt. MacDonald provided Mr. Ayala-Powell the Incident #, all of the Officers Names/Badge Numbers, as well as how to make a record request for Body Worn Camera footage. Mr. Ayala-Powell then informed me and Sgt. Macdonald " I have everything I need; I really appreciate your help."  I then provided Mr. Ayala-Powell my department card, badge number, as well as my contact information. Mr. Ayala-Powell then left District B-3. ¶ Following the conversation at District B-3, I proceeded to the Carney Hospital to speak with Ms. Pizarro in regard to this incident. I (Sgt. Gomes) then photographed Ms. Pizarro's physical injuries. I then spoke to the medical staff at the Carney Hospital as well. I provided Ms. Pizarro with my department card, badge number, as well as my contact information. ¶ Due to the Initial statements made by both Mr. Ayala-Powell, Ms. Pizarro, as well as speaking to the Officers involved in this incident, I, (Sgt. Gomes) am making this notification into the Blue Notes system. I, (Sgt. Gomes) will conduct a Use of Force investigation into this incident and will be further investigated.

It was a domestic call that that was a verbal dispute between my resident and her significant other.. The officers (2) had ask for some assistance due to the significant other yelling and refusing to leave. Not once did this report say that this gentleman was causing any harm or attempting to cause harm to anyone else. There was 5 or 6 officers whom is seen on video running into the building and none of the officers called or rang the doorbell to the actual unit nor did they ring anyone else door to be let in. Within 1- 2 min an officer took out his flashlight and busted the glass door after trying to yank the door open. I understand an officers job, when someone is being threatened or harmed, however this was not the case no one was in any imminent danger nor did anyone physically fight with the officers to make them feel that this was warranted.They was asked by the residents on the fist floor why didn't they ring the doorbell not one officer respond with an answer or an apology. The worst part of this is our telephone # is posted in that same vestibule and not one of your officers stayed on scene to ensure no one coming in or out of the building was hurt from the glass that was still falling from the door while they waited for management to send someone to clean up. This is unacceptable and I feel the officer should be reprimanded and should come out of pocket and pay for the replacement himself.The officer's should be ashamed of themselves. We deserve an explanation as to why such excessive force was used and how the BPD will correct the behavior of their officers who felt no responsibility to reach out to us to provide a solution to a now damaged door. Clearly they could see that once the glass was broken none of us were safe from L***y or anyone else who may have wanted to access the building. The BPD needs to do better.

At approximately 21:41 hours on Monday, August 17, 2020 Officers Michael McNulty and James Gigliello in the L101F were dispatched to 53 Fairmount Ave in Hyde Park for a fight call.  Upon arrival the responding officers encountered a group of people arguing including off duty Police Officer Carmen Padron and off duty Boston Health and Hospitals EMT Aimee Perez.  While onscene Padron proceeded to push her ex-boyfriend in the presence of the officers  The officers did not take any information from the persons on scene, complete an incident report or notify the patrol supervisor of an incident involving an off duty Boston Police Officer.  The officers ordered the group to leave the area without further action being taken. ¶ A short time later Perez responded to District 18 where she requested that front desk Officer Jessica Anderson write a police report documenting the incident.  Perez stated that the responding officers focused their attention on Officer Padron, did not aske her for any information and one yelled at the group to get the fuck out of there. ¶ Criminal complaints were filed and charges issued for Padron for the assault and battery. On today's date, January 27, 2026, I was assigned as the day shift Lieutenant, HA02.  At the 7:30 roll call, I observed that Officer Dale Kennedy was not wearing a uniform shirt.  He was wearing a fleece with his badge attached to it, and a turtleneck.  I told Officer Kennedy (the last time I saw him) that he needs to wear a uniform shirt.  Officer Kennedy explained prior that putting a uniform shirt on would have made him late for roll call, and he expected to change clothes after roll call.  I told him that he needs to appear at roll call in full uniform.  For that reason, on today's date, I was surprised to see Officer Kennedy without a uniform shirt on again, so I mentioned again that he needs to wear a uniform shirt.  I typically mention it at roll call or whenever I happen to notice that someone is wearing an unauthorized hat, no hat, or otherwise out of uniform. ¶ After roll call, Sgt. Matthew Walsh and I were in the Duty Supervisor's office.  Officer Dale Kennedy stepped into the D.S. office, and without asking permission to do so, closed the supervisor office door behind him.  Officer Kennedy expressed that he felt "targeted" because he has been on the day shift "for a long time," and he was not the only person he has seen out of uniform on the shift.  He inquired if I would prefer that he "have a shirt on, or be late for roll call?"  I thought it was interesting that he wanted me to choose out of the two options.  I told him that I want him to do both, to be on time for roll call and to be in proper uniform.  Officer Kennedy was standing there having the conversation with me while wearing no uniform shirt, and an unauthorized winter watch cap with unknown logo on the front. I spoke to officers at roll call after the recent clothing allowance being paid, and they were all put on notice to fix the uniform issues. ¶ Several other officers on my shift (and on other shifts) have been spoken to by me individually or at roll call about their appearance since I've been at C-11 (usually hats and shirts).  Not one of them besides Officer Kennedy has come into the D.S. office to complain about what they were told.  Further, it is none of Officer Kennedy's business what my communication with other officers might have been regarding their appearance.  I do not answer to Officer Kennedy, but he seems to think so.  Officer Kennedy was recently assigned to be an FTO training a probationary officer.  All officers at roll call were spoken to prior about being an example for the new officers who are in training. ¶ Officer Kennedy has issues with time management on a consistent basis (late for his shift).  But most surprising to me is that he refuses to follow my directives when he is told to show up to roll call in proper uniform.  And, he seems offended by being corrected regarding that.  Further, he seems entitled to dictate a meeting with me to discuss it while choosing the time and place to have that conversation. Also, Officer Kennedy seems to think it is appropriate to ask me to negotiate whether I want him to follow one rule, or the other, as if I am in a position to choose only one rule for him to follow.  I expressed to Captain Sweeney (C-11 Commander) my issues with Officer Kennedy, that he will be writing a Form 26 report regarding our conversation, and that my opinion he is definitely not suitable to train a probationary officer who just graduated from the Academy. ¶ Officer Kennedy failed to show up in proper uniform in violation of Rule 103 Section 3, he refused to follow my directive to show up to roll call in proper uniform Rule 102, Section 8, and he walked into the D.S. office to complain about the directive with a sense of entitlement to do so as though he runs my shift.  Officer Kennedy was disrespectful.  On one occasion, I was meeting with an officer and a supervisor in my office.  I hung a sign on the door, stating that I was busy, and indicated where to leave any paperwork or messages for me.  Officer Kennedy disregarded the sign, and interrupted the meeting by knocking on the door, simply to hand me a Form 25. Further, it is none of Officer Kennedy's business what my communication with other officers might have been regarding their appearance.  I do not answer to Officer Kennedy, but he seems to think so.  Officer Kennedy was recently assigned to be an FTO training a probationary officer.  All officers at roll call were spoken to prior about being an example for the new officers who are in training. ¶ Officer Kennedy has issues with time management on a consistent basis (late for his shift).  But most surprising to me is that he refuses to follow my directives when he is told to show up to roll call in proper uniform.  And, he seems offended by being corrected regarding that.  Further, he seems entitled to dictate a meeting with me to discuss it while choosing the time and place to have that conversation. Also, Officer Kennedy seems to think it is appropriate to ask me to negotiate whether I want him to follow one rule, or the other, as if I am in a position to choose only one rule for him to follow.  I expressed to Captain Sweeney (C-11 Commander) my issues with Officer Kennedy, that he will be writing a Form 26 report regarding our conversation, and that my opinion he is definitely not suitable to train a probationary officer who just graduated from the Academy. ¶ Officer Kennedy failed to show up in proper uniform in violation of Rule 103 Section 3, he refused to follow my directive to show up to roll call in proper uniform Rule 102, Section 8, and he walked into the D.S. office to complain about the directive with a sense of entitlement to do so as though he runs my shift. Complainant Jaqueline Tucker called Internal Affairs and spoke with the on-call investigator to file a complaint. She stated that on Tuesday February 18, 2020 at approximately 11:30 am, she ordered a Lyft to pick her up on Amory St, E-13. A verbal disagreement ensued between the complainant and the Lyft driver about her pick-up location. Ms. Tucker stated that driver called 911. Two Hispanic officers from E-13 responded. While on-scene, the officers and Lyft driver were speaking Spanish which the complainant did not like. Ms.Tucker further reported that she asked that the Officers to force the Lyft driver to speak English, to which they ignored. She stated that she was removed from the vehicle. Additionally, when she asked for his name and badge number, the Officer refused to identify himself. Ms. Tucker stated that she did not like the treatment she received and intends to retain a lawyer. ¶ Complainant Jaqueline Tucker called Internal Affairs and spoke with the on-call investigator to file a complaint.
